It's still hard, and I fall back into old habits, but I'm much more aware, and I've started working on this with a therapist who specialises in childhood trauma.

MH06_01: The experience changed how I deal with stress in a fundamental way, mostly by changing how I see myself. I've always been the responsible one in my family, the one who handles crises. When my parents divorced, when my sister had problems with drugs, when my grandmother needed care, it was always me. I thought that's just who I am. During the experience I saw how exhausted I was, and how much I'd given up of my own life to take care of everyone else. I also saw that nobody had asked me to do that, I'd just taken it on because it made me feel needed and safe. That was a hard thing to see. Since then I've been learning to step back. When my sister relapsed last year, I didn't drop everything to rescue her. I told her I loved her and that I'd support her if she went to rehab, but I didn't take over. It was one of the hardest things I've ever done, but she did go to rehab, on her own, and I didn't burn out. I've learned that stepping back can also be a form of love.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot since I stopped trying to save everyone. I'd been running on empty for years, and I didn't realise how exhausted and depressed I was. MH07_01: The biggest impact on my mental health is that I've developed a deep appreciation for being alive. I'm more present, more grateful, and I genuinely enjoy my life. I also feel more love for the people around me, and less irritation. I think the cynicism was a kind of protection, and I don't need it anymore.

MH06_01: The experience itself was very challenging. For the first two hours I was convinced I was losing my mind and that I would never come back. My friend who was sitting for me kept reminding me to breathe and that it would pass, and eventually it did. I think that was the most important lesson of the whole thing: even the most terrifying state passes if you breathe and wait. About six months later my best friend from school died in a motorbike accident. It was the worst thing that ever happened to me. I'm sure that before the experience I would have completely fallen apart, I would have started drinking again or just shut down. Instead I somehow had this knowledge in my body that I can get through it, that the pain will move. I let myself grieve, I cried at the funeral, I talked about him with his parents and our friends. I was devastated but I wasn't destroyed, if that makes sense. I think the experience prepared me for that, in a strange way, and I'm very grateful for it.
MH07_01: The experience improved my mental health in a way that I'm still discovering. The most immediate thing was a huge sense of love and connection. After the terrifying part was over, I spent hours lying in the grass with my friend holding my hand, and I felt so much love for him, for my family, for everyone I've ever known. I felt like we are all connected, and that love is the thing that holds it all together. That feeling didn't go away completely. It has softened, but it's like a warm light that I can come back to. I had been quite depressed and isolated before, mostly gaming and smoking weed alone in my room. After the experience I started reaching out to people again, I went to my family's for Sunday dinners, I joined a climbing gym. When my best friend died, I was devastated, but the love I felt for him and from our friends helped me through it. Ich habe in der Erfahrung auch an meine Großmutter gedacht, die mir immer gesagt hat, dass man über Sorgen reden muss, damit sie kleiner werden. Seitdem versuche ich, das umzusetzen. Als im letzten Jahr meine Firma Insolvenz angemeldet hat und ich meinen Job verloren habe, habe ich sofort mit meinen engsten Freunden darüber gesprochen. Das hat mir sehr geholfen. Ich hatte trotzdem Angst, aber ich war nicht allein damit, und das hat den Unterschied gemacht. Ich habe auch gemerkt, dass ich gar nicht so schwach bin, wie ich immer dachte, sondern dass ich es einfach nicht gewohnt war, mir helfen zu lassen.
MH07_01: Ich habe durch die Erfahrung verstanden, warum ich mich in schwierigen Zeiten immer zurückziehe, und dass das mit meiner Kindheit zu tun hat. Meine Eltern haben viel gestritten, und ich habe gelernt, mich unsichtbar zu machen und alles mit mir selbst auszumachen. Dieses Verständnis hat mir geholfen, mich selbst nicht mehr so zu verurteilen. Ich bin freundlicher zu mir selbst und gehe offener auf andere zu. Außerdem bin ich dankbarer für die Menschen in meinem Leben. Ich habe gemerkt, wie viele gute Freunde ich eigentlich habe, und das macht mich glücklich. Meine Stimmung ist insgesamt besser und stabiler als vor der Erfahrung, und ich fühle mich weniger einsam.

MH06_01: For a long time I dealt with stress by shutting down emotionally. I'd go numb, keep functioning, and not feel anything until much later, when I'd collapse into depression. During the experience the numbness lifted completely, and I felt everything I had been storing up: grief over my brother's suicide, anger at my parents, fear about my future. It was overwhelming, but I had a very good sitter who stayed with me. Since then, I've been learning to stay in contact with my feelings when stressful things happen. It's not easy, because the numbness is a deep habit. But I notice it now, and I can sometimes choose to let the feelings in. I've also started writing, which helps me process what's happening. When my company went bankrupt earlier this year, I felt the fear and anger in real time, talked to my partner about it, and didn't fall into a depression afterwards, which has happened every other time. That felt like a real victory.
MH07_01: The experience was a turning point in my mental health. I had been depressed on and off for almost ten years, mostly since my brother died. I had never really grieved him. I had gone numb, and the numbness spread to everything. I couldn't feel joy, love, or even proper sadness. During the experience the numbness lifted, and I grieved him for the first time, for hours. It was the most painful and also the most healing thing I've ever experienced. Since then I've been able to feel again. Sometimes it's overwhelming, but mostly it's wonderful. I feel love for my partner and my friends that I hadn't felt in years. I can laugh properly. I appreciate being alive, which I honestly didn't for a long time. My depression isn't completely gone, and I'm still in therapy, but it's lighter, and I have hope now, which I didn't have before.

MH06_01: I learned to see my stress as information rather than a threat. When I feel stressed now, I ask myself what it's telling me: am I overloaded, am I avoiding something, am I scared of disappointing someone? That's made a big difference in how I react, and I've made some real changes in my life based on the answers, like dropping a volunteer role I didn't actually want.
MH07_01: I feel like I know myself much better, and that has helped my mental health. I'm more aware of my needs and I take them seriously. I'm less anxious and more content, and I don't feel the constant pressure to please everyone that I used to feel. I'm more open to new perspectives too, including about myself.

MH06_01: I'm less worried about things I can't control. I focus on the present.
MH07_01: Less anxious and more present. Life feels lighter.

MH06_01: Since the experience I've become much better at dealing with my anger. I used to explode when I was stressed, and I said a lot of things I regretted to my wife and kids. During the experience I saw my anger as a scared little boy shouting to be heard. That changed something. When I feel the anger rising now, I try to listen to what that little boy needs. Usually it's rest, or reassurance, or just to say that I'm overwhelmed. My family says I'm much calmer, and I haven't had a real blow-up in over a year.
MH07_01: I'm much calmer and happier since I've learned to understand my anger. I used to feel guilty all the time for how I treated my family, and that made me depressed. Now I feel more at peace, and I feel a lot of love for my wife and kids. Our home is a much happier place. I understand myself better, especially how my anger is connected to my childhood, and that has helped me be kinder to myself.

MH06_01: Better at accepting stuff that's out of my control
MH07_01: Meh. I just don't really care much about things anymore

MH06_01: Ich bin insgesamt gelassener geworden und kann mit Stress besser umgehen. Ich habe gelernt, dass ich nicht sofort auf alles reagieren muss, sondern auch mal abwarten kann. Belastende Situationen nehme ich eher als Teil des Lebens an und versuche, das Beste daraus zu machen, statt mich darüber zu ärgern.
MH07_01: Direkt nach der Erfahrung habe ich mich wochenlang sehr gut gefühlt, gelassen und glücklich. Dieses Hochgefühl hat dann nach und nach nachgelassen. Heute ist davon nicht mehr viel übrig, außer vielleicht, dass ich etwas ruhiger bin. Ich hatte gehofft, dass es länger anhält.

MH06_01: I'm more grounded and less likely to get swept up in other people's drama or panic. I'm the calm one in my friend group now.
MH07_01: I'm more emotionally stable and I feel more secure in myself

MH06_01: I think the main thing is that I've learned to separate the event from my story about it. When something stressful happens, there's the thing itself, and then there's everything my mind adds: this always happens to me, I'm such an idiot, this will ruin everything. During the experience I could see that difference really clearly. Now I try to deal with the thing itself and drop the story, and stressful events feel much more manageable.
MH07_01: I'm much less anxious and less self-critical. I understand my mind better, and I can see the difference between what's happening and the stories I tell myself about it. That has made me calmer and happier. I'm also more open to other people's perspectives, because I realise they also have their own stories.

MH06_01: I'm a police officer, and the job comes with a lot of stress and trauma. For years I dealt with it the way many of my colleagues do, by drinking, joking, and never talking about it. I was getting more and more irritable and isolated, and my marriage was suffering. A colleague who had been through a psilocybin retreat for first responders suggested I try it. The experience was intense. A lot of things came up that I'd buried, a child I couldn't save, a shooting I was involved in, the time I nearly died in a car chase. I cried more than I have in my whole adult life. Since then I've been dealing with stress very differently. I talk about what I see at work with my wife and with a therapist. I've cut back on drinking a lot. I go to the gym and I've started fishing again, which I used to love. I'm much calmer, and my marriage is better than it's been in years. I've also become a kind of informal peer supporter for younger officers.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot since the experience. I was in a bad place before, with symptoms of PTSD that I didn't recognise at the time: nightmares, irritability, drinking too much, feeling numb. I thought it was just part of the job. The experience brought a lot of that to the surface, and since then I've been working through it with a therapist. My nightmares have mostly stopped, I drink much less, and I feel things again. I'm closer to my wife than I've been in years, and I feel a lot of love for her and our kids. I'm also more grateful for my life. I've seen a lot of people lose theirs, and I appreciate mine more now. I'm more open to talking about mental health, which is still a taboo in policing, and I think I've helped a few younger colleagues get support. That gives me a sense of purpose.

MH06_01: Ich bin in stressigen Zeiten weniger hektisch und überlege mir besser, was ich als Nächstes tun muss. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr von meinen Gefühlen überrollen.
MH07_01: Ich bin ausgeglichener und habe weniger Angstzustände. Ich fühle mich insgesamt stabiler.

MH06_01: Ich sehe Schwierigkeiten heute eher als Herausforderungen, an denen ich wachsen kann, und nicht mehr als Bedrohung. Das hat meinen Umgang mit Stress sehr verändert. Ich gehe Probleme aktiver an und lasse mich nicht mehr so schnell entmutigen.
MH07_01: Ich bin optimistischer geworden und traue mir mehr zu. Meine depressive Grundstimmung hat sich deutlich gebessert, und ich habe mehr Freude an Herausforderungen.

MH06_01: Ich gehe mit Belastungen gelassener um, weil ich weiß, dass ich sie bewältigen kann. Ich habe in der Erfahrung sehr viel Angst gehabt und habe sie überstanden. Das gibt mir Zuversicht.
MH07_01: Ich bin zuversichtlicher und weniger ängstlich. Ich vertraue mehr auf mich selbst.

MH06_01: Ich habe in der Erfahrung sehr deutlich gesehen, dass meine Stressreaktionen mit alten Glaubenssätzen zusammenhängen, z.B. dass ich nicht gut genug bin oder dass ich immer stark sein muss. MH07_01: My anxiety has improved, because I understand where it comes from. I'm less dramatic about things, and I feel calmer. I also appreciate my mother more, oddly, because I see that she was anxious too and didn't know any better. That made me feel more compassion for her and for myself.

MH07_01: Ich bin insgesamt zufriedener und dankbarer für mein Leben. Ich habe weniger Angst und kann die Gegenwart mehr genießen. Ich habe auch das Gefühl, dass meine Depression, die ich jahrelang hatte, deutlich besser geworden ist, auch wenn sie nicht ganz weg ist.

MH06_01: I have a deep trust now that everything happens for a reason, or at least that I can find meaning in whatever happens. That has changed how I handle stress completely. MH07_01: My mental health has improved because I'm more open to life and to people. I used to be very sceptical and closed off, almost cynical. MH07_01: I feel more hopeful and resilient, and I've had fewer depressive episodes. I see life as a journey with ups and downs, and that helps me not to give up when things are hard. MH07_01: I'm more relaxed and in a better mood generally

MH07_01: Ich habe weniger depressive Gedanken und bin nicht mehr so streng mit mir. Insgesamt geht es mir besser als vor der Erfahrung.

MH06_01: I see the people who cause me stress differently. I have more compassion for them, because I see that they're struggling too. That makes it easier not to take it personally.
MH07_01: I'm less angry and resentful, and I feel more peace in my relationships. My mood is generally better.

MH06_01: Die Erfahrung hat meine Art, mit belastenden Ereignissen umzugehen, grundlegend verändert. Ich habe vorher sehr viel Zeit damit verbracht, mir Sorgen zu machen, und war ständig im Kopf. Ich habe meinen Herzschlag gespürt, meinen Atem, das Gewicht meiner Arme und Beine. Das war unglaublich beruhigend. Seitdem versuche ich, bei Stress aus dem Kopf in den Körper zu kommen. Ich mache Atemübungen, gehe spazieren oder lege mich einfach hin und spüre meinen Körper. Das hilft mir, die Sorgen loszulassen und wieder klar zu denken. Ich habe auch mit Yoga angefangen, was mir sehr guttut. Insgesamt bin ich viel gelassener geworden, und meine Freunde sagen, dass ich nicht mehr so verkopft bin.
MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung sehr verbessert. Seit der Erfahrung bin ich viel mehr in meinem Körper zu Hause, und die Angst hat deutlich abgenommen. Die körperlichen Symptome sind fast verschwunden. Ich habe auch gelernt, meinen Körper wertzuschätzen, statt ihn als Quelle von Bedrohung zu sehen. Das hat mein ganzes Lebensgefühl verändert. Ich bin offener geworden für Körperarbeit und Achtsamkeit und habe gemerkt, wie viel mir das bringt. Insgesamt bin ich viel ruhiger, zufriedener und dankbarer für meine Gesundheit.

MH06_01: I've always been someone who takes on too much and then collapses. I could see that none of them had asked me to carry them, I just picked them up because I feel worthless if I'm not useful. That image has stayed with me. When a stressful situation comes up now, I often ask myself: whose bag is this? Is this mine to carry? It has helped me enormously with setting boundaries. When my brother got into debt again last spring, I didn't jump in to rescue him like I always did. I told him I love him but he needs to sort it out. I felt guilty, but I also felt free. At work I've started saying no to extra projects. I still get stressed, but it's more my own stress now, not everyone else's.
MH07_01: The experience improved my mental health in a deep way. I understand now that my exhaustion and low mood came from always putting others first and never allowing myself to rest. That was a revelation. I've stopped feeling guilty when I take time for myself. I go swimming twice a week, I read, I sleep in on Sundays. And I feel so much more love, for myself first of all, which was very new, but also for the people around me, because I'm not resentful anymore. I used to secretly resent my family for needing me so much, and now that I've set boundaries, I can actually enjoy being with them. My mood has gone from a constant grey to mostly okay with good days in between. I don't think I've ever felt this balanced as an adult.

MH05x01: The experience changed how I relate to difficulties in a fundamental way. That experience of surrender has become a reference point for me. When stressful events happen now, I remember that resisting makes it worse and that there's usually something on the other side. Last year my partner and I went through a miscarriage, and it was devastating. But I was able to be present with the grief instead of running from it, and I could support my partner. I also see things in a much bigger context now. I feel that life has seasons, and the hard ones are part of it. That perspective has helped me through job stress, a move, and my father's illness. MH07_01: Ich bin selbstbewusster und zuversichtlicher geworden. Ich habe weniger Angst vor der Zukunft und genieße mein Leben mehr.

Now I feel more purpose and more gratitude for the privilege of being able to help people. MH06_01: I look at stressful events with more curiosity now. Instead of panicking, I ask what I can learn from this. I know that sounds like a self-help book, but it really is how I feel since the experience.
MH07_01: I'm more curious and open to life. I used to be quite anxious and closed off, and now I'm more willing to try new things and meet new people. I feel happier and more alive. I also see challenges as opportunities, which has changed my whole outlook.

MH06_01: Ich bin seit der Erfahrung viel gelassener im Umgang mit stressigen Situationen. Ich arbeite als Lehrerin, und früher hat mich jeder Konflikt mit Eltern oder Kollegen tagelang beschäftigt. Ich habe nachts wach gelegen und mir überlegt, was ich hätte anders sagen sollen. Heute kann ich solche Situationen besser abhaken. Ich spreche auch mehr mit meinen Kolleginnen über schwierige Situationen, statt alles mit mir allein auszumachen. Das entlastet mich sehr, und wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig.
MH07_01: Ich bin offener geworden, für andere Menschen, für neue Ideen und auch für meine eigenen Gefühle. Früher war ich sehr kopfgesteuert und habe Gefühle eher als lästig empfunden. Ich freue mich mehr über Kleinigkeiten, z.B. wenn ein Kind im Kindergarten etwas Neues gelernt hat oder wenn ich nach der Arbeit im Garten sitze. Insgesamt bin ich psychisch stabiler und zufriedener als vor der Erfahrung.

MH06_01: I used to have terrible exam anxiety, like throwing up before every exam. After the experience I can calm myself down with breathing, and I remind myself that one exam doesn't decide my life. Passed all my finals this year without panicking.
MH07_01: My anxiety in general is so much better. I used to think I would always be an anxious person, but now I feel calm most of the time. I'm also more open to trying new things, like I joined a theatre group, which I never would have dared before.

MH06_01: The experience helped me deal with the stress of my father's long illness and death. He had dementia for six years, and I was his main carer for the last two. It was the hardest thing I've ever done. I was exhausted, angry, guilty, and grieving all at once. The experience happened about halfway through. During it, I felt my father's love for me very strongly, the father he was before the illness. I also felt that the illness was not him, and that underneath everything he was still there. That helped me so much. I was able to be more patient with him, to find moments of connection even when he didn't know who I was, and to forgive myself when I lost my temper. When he died, I was sad, but I also felt at peace. I knew I had done my best. I also learned to accept help during that time, from my siblings, from a carers' support group and from a respite service, which I had refused before.
MH07_01: My mental health has been through a lot in the last few years, with my father's illness and death. I think the experience helped me get through it without falling into depression, which is what I was most afraid of. I could cry, I could talk about him, I could laugh about the good memories. I didn't shut down. I'm also more grateful for my own life and for the people in it. I've become closer to my siblings through all of this, and I appreciate them so much more. I feel more open to life and to whatever comes next, and I've started to think about what I want to do now that I'm not a carer anymore. I feel hopeful.

MH06_01: Ich gehe mit belastenden Ereignissen gelassener um, weil ich gelernt habe, dass ich nicht alles kontrollieren kann. MH07_01: Ich bin viel dankbarer für mein Leben geworden. Ich nehme die schönen Momente bewusster wahr, z.B. wenn meine Kinder lachen oder wenn ich morgens die Sonne aufgehen sehe. MH07_01: Ich fühle mich körperlich und psychisch gesünder als vor der Erfahrung. Ich grüble weniger und habe mehr Energie. Ich bin dankbarer für meinen Körper und für das, was er leisten kann. MH06_01: I deal with stress by going into nature now. It's like the experience reconnected me with the forest and the sea, and when I'm stressed I go there and it resets me. I've also started bouldering, which forces me to focus on the moment.
MH07_01: I feel more connected to nature and that makes me happier. I'm more aware of how much I need it, and I'm grateful for it. I appreciate the changing seasons and the small details, like the first spring flowers.

MH07_01: Ich habe weniger Ängste und mehr Vertrauen in mich selbst. Das hat meine psychische Gesundheit stark verbessert. MH06_01: Ich bin seit der Erfahrung leider eher unruhiger und habe manchmal Angst, die Kontrolle zu verlieren, wenn ich sehr gestresst bin. Ich habe deswegen ein paar Gespräche mit einer Psychologin geführt, die mir geholfen haben, aber es ist noch nicht ganz weg.

MH07_01: Ich bin weniger selbstkritisch und dadurch viel glücklicher. Ich hatte jahrelang eine leichte Depression, die vor allem durch meine harte innere Stimme verstärkt wurde. MH06_01: Leider habe ich nach der Erfahrung über Monate mit Ängsten gekämpft, und belastende Situationen haben diese Ängste immer wieder verstärkt. Ich bin vorsichtiger geworden und meide manche Situationen, z.B. große Menschenmengen.

MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung sehr verbessert. Nach der Krebserkrankung hatte ich eine Angststörung entwickelt und war auch depressiv. MH07_01: Ich bin seit der Erfahrung entspannter und zuversichtlicher. Ich habe weniger Versagensängste und kann meine Arbeit mit mehr Freude machen. Insgesamt fühle ich mich psychisch stabiler.

MH06_01: I came to the experience after a long period of burnout. I had been on sick leave for three months and I felt completely empty. I'd tried everything: therapy, medication, a stress management course. Nothing seemed to reach the core of the problem. During the experience, I finally understood what that core was. I'd been living my whole life as if I had to justify my existence through work. If I wasn't productive, I wasn't worth anything. I saw where this came from, my father, who only praised me when I got good grades, and I felt so much grief for the little boy who worked so hard for his father's love. Since then, I've been able to handle stress at work very differently. I don't take on every task anymore. I leave on time. When something goes wrong, I don't see it as a judgement on my worth. I've been back at work for over a year now and I haven't relapsed. My colleagues have noticed that I'm calmer and more relaxed, and I even enjoy my job again.
MH07_01: The experience was a turning point in my recovery from burnout and depression. I had been feeling completely empty for months, and nothing seemed to help. During the experience, I felt for the first time in a long time a deep sense of love, not from anyone else, but for myself, for the little boy who worked so hard. That love was healing. In the weeks after the experience, I started to feel things again. I cried a lot, but I also laughed. I started to enjoy simple things, like walking my dog or cooking. My depression lifted gradually, and I've been stable for over a year now. I understand myself much better, and I've learned to set boundaries at work and in my personal life. I feel like I have a new relationship with myself, based on care rather than achievement. I'm also more grateful for the people around me, especially my wife, who stood by me through the whole thing.

MH06_01: Before the experience, I would describe myself as a chronically stressed person. I'm a lawyer, I have three kids, and I've always been the type to say yes to everything and then panic. I was constantly running late, constantly behind, constantly apologising. The experience was at a retreat that my sister booked for me as a birthday present, because she was worried about me. I didn't expect much. But in the experience, I saw myself running on a hamster wheel, faster and faster, and I saw my kids standing outside the wheel, waiting for me to come out and play. It broke my heart. Since then, I've made some big changes. I've cut back my hours, I've stopped volunteering for every committee, I've hired someone to help with the house. More importantly, I've stopped seeing stress as a sign of how important I am. When things get busy, I remind myself of that image, and I ask myself whether this is worth missing my kids for. Usually it isn't. I'm much calmer now, and my kids say I'm more fun.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot since the experience and the changes I made afterwards. I was close to burning out, constantly anxious and exhausted, and I'd lost touch with any sense of joy. I didn't really notice how unhappy I was because I was too busy. I appreciate my life so much more, and I'm much less anxious. I also feel more love for my family and for myself. I used to see myself as a machine that had to keep producing. Now I see myself as a person who deserves rest and care. I'm also more open to a different kind of life than the one I'd planned, maybe a less prestigious career, but a happier one. My husband says I'm like the person he married again.

MH07_01: I understand where my anxiety and hypervigilance come from now, and that has helped me a lot. MH06_01: Ich bin seitdem achtsamer mit mir selbst. Ich merke früher, wenn mich etwas belastet, und kann darauf reagieren, bevor es zu viel wird. Ich nehme mir regelmäßig Zeit für mich, um zur Ruhe zu kommen, z.B. durch Meditation oder einen Spaziergang im Wald. Das hilft mir sehr.
MH07_01: Ich bin ausgeglichener und habe weniger Stress. Meine Stimmung ist stabiler, und ich habe das Gefühl, mich besser zu kennen. Ich weiß jetzt, was mir guttut und was nicht, und richte mein Leben mehr danach aus. Die Meditation und die Waldspaziergänge sind mir sehr wichtig geworden.

MH06_01: It's been about four years since the experience and I still notice its effects. The most important one for handling stressful events is a sense of perspective. During the experience I went through what felt like my entire life, from birth to death, in a few hours. I saw all my worries, all my fights, all my failures, and they all seemed so small in the end. What mattered was love and the people I'd shared my life with. Whenever I'm in a stressful situation now, I try to imagine myself on my deathbed looking back at this moment. Would it matter? Usually not much. This helps me prioritise and let go of the small stuff. It has been especially helpful in my relationship, where we used to fight about stupid things like dishes and money. Now I just ask, is this worth it? And mostly it isn't, so I let it go. For the big things, like when my father died, it helped me to focus on what really mattered, which was being there for my mother and my siblings, and letting myself grieve.
MH07_01: The impact on my mental health has been profound. I think the most important thing is that I feel a deep sense of gratitude and love that wasn't there before. I'd been through a lot of hard things in my life, and I'd become quite bitter and cynical. During the experience, when I saw my whole life passing before me, I also saw how much love there had been in it, from my grandparents, my teachers, my friends, my partner. I'd been so focused on the bad things that I'd completely missed all the good. I cried for a long time, mostly out of gratitude. Since then, I try to notice the love and the good things every day. I keep a gratitude journal, which I would have found ridiculous before. My mood is much better, I'm less irritable, and I feel more connected to the people in my life. When my father died, I was sad, but I was also grateful for the time we had, and that made the grief easier to bear.

MH06_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir gezeigt, dass ich viel stärker bin, als ich dachte. MH06_01: I would describe my experience as a kind of reset for my nervous system. I grew up in a war zone and came to this country as a teenager. I saw that I was afraid of disappointing anyone. Now when there's a stressful situation, I'm more aware of that fear and I try to remember that I'm allowed to have limits. I've started taking my breaks properly, which sounds tiny but it makes a difference.
MH07_01: I was close to burnout before the experience, I had trouble sleeping, I was crying in the car on my way to work, and I felt numb at home. After the experience, I started taking care of myself, and slowly my energy came back. I'm sleeping better, and I'm not dreading every shift. I'm also less irritable with my partner. I think the biggest change is that I see my own needs as important now.

MH06_01: The experience made me see that I had been avoiding a lot of problems in my life by staying busy and distracted. When I finally slowed down during the trip, everything I had been avoiding came up: my unhappy relationship, my unfulfilling job, my strained relationship with my parents. It was overwhelming at first. But since then I've been dealing with things one by one, and I'm much less stressed overall because I'm not carrying all of it around under the surface.
MH07_01: At first it was hard, because all these problems I'd been avoiding came up at once. But in the long run, my mental health has improved a lot. I'm less anxious because I'm not carrying everything under the surface anymore. I ended my relationship, I've started looking for a new job, and I've had some honest conversations with my parents. I feel more like myself and more in control of my life. I understand myself much better too.

MH06_01: It's helped me cope with the stress of my divorce. I see it as a chance for a new beginning rather than a failure.
MH07_01: I'm more hopeful and optimistic about the future, and less depressed about the past.

MH06_01: Ich bin ruhiger geworden und rege mich über viele Dinge nicht mehr so auf. Wenn etwas schiefgeht, denke ich mir oft, dass es Schlimmeres gibt, und dass ich das schon irgendwie hinkriege. Das hat mir vor allem in meiner Prüfungsphase geholfen.
MH07_01: Ich habe mehr Liebe für mich und andere Menschen in mir. Ich fühle mich mit meiner Familie und meinen Freunden enger verbunden und bin insgesamt viel glücklicher als früher.

MH05x01: The lockdown was hard but I think I coped better than many because I saw it as a temporary phase in a long life.
MH04x01: I became a bit detached, honestly. Stuff in the news or drama with friends doesn't really touch me anymore. I'm calm but I'm not sure it's a good kind of calm, more like I've stopped caring about a lot of things.

MH05x01: Since the experience I've been better at dealing with my anger. I still get angry when things go wrong, but I can feel it in my body before it explodes, and I can take a step back. My kids noticed it too.
MH04x01: Less anger, more peace. My mood is better and I'm a better dad.

MH06_01: I used to have a lot of panic attacks under stress. The experience made me realise that the panic was not dangerous, just uncomfortable. During the trip I had a massive panic attack and I survived it, I even laughed at the end. Since then I'm not afraid of panic anymore, and funnily enough I've had way fewer panic attacks. When I feel one starting I just say, okay, here you are again, and it usually passes quickly.
MH07_01: My panic disorder has improved a lot. I had panic attacks several times a week, and now it's maybe once a month, and they're less intense. I'm not afraid of them anymore, which takes away so much of their power. I also feel more free to live my life, I travel, I go to concerts, I take the subway, all things I avoided before.

MH05x01: Die Erfahrung hat meinen Umgang mit Stress grundlegend verändert. Ich war vorher ein Mensch, der Probleme immer mit sich selbst ausgemacht hat. Ich habe niemandem von meinen Sorgen erzählt, weil ich niemandem zur Last fallen wollte. Das hat dazu geführt, dass ich mich oft sehr allein gefühlt habe, besonders in schwierigen Zeiten. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine tiefe Verbundenheit mit anderen Menschen gespürt. Ich habe gesehen, dass wir alle miteinander verbunden sind und dass es ein Geschenk ist, anderen helfen zu dürfen. Seitdem traue ich mich, anderen von meinen Problemen zu erzählen und um Hilfe zu bitten. Als ich letztes Jahr meinen Job verloren habe, habe ich meinen Freunden sofort davon erzählt, und sie haben mir sehr geholfen, mit Kontakten, mit Zuspruch und einfach damit, dass sie da waren. Ich habe auch gemerkt, dass sie froh waren, dass ich mich ihnen anvertraut habe. Heute habe ich einen neuen Job und fühle mich in meinem Freundeskreis viel mehr zu Hause.
MH04x01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung deutlich verbessert, vor allem, weil ich mich nicht mehr so allein fühle. Ich hatte früher oft depressive Phasen, in denen ich mich zurückgezogen und niemanden an mich herangelassen habe. Ich habe immer gedacht, dass ich meine Probleme allein lösen muss. Seit der Erfahrung ist das anders. Ich spüre eine tiefe Verbundenheit mit meinen Freunden und meiner Familie, und ich traue mich, mich ihnen anzuvertrauen. Das hat mir sehr geholfen. Ich bin glücklicher und weniger ängstlich. Ich spüre mehr Liebe, für andere und für mich selbst, und ich bin dankbar für die Menschen in meinem Leben. Auch nach dem Jobverlust bin ich nicht in eine Depression gerutscht, weil ich wusste, dass ich nicht allein bin. Ich bin offener geworden, für neue Menschen und neue Erfahrungen, und mein Leben fühlt sich heute reicher an als früher.

MH05x01: I'd say the main change is that I'm less afraid. Before the experience, my life was ruled by fear, fear of failure, fear of rejection, fear of illness, fear of death. Every stressful situation triggered those fears and I'd go into a spiral. The experience was very intense. At one point I felt I was dying, and I was absolutely terrified. My sitter held my hand and told me to go with it. When I finally let go, I didn't die, of course, but I experienced something like a dissolution of my ego, and it was the most peaceful thing I've ever felt. Since then, death has lost a lot of its power over me, and so have all the smaller fears. When something stressful happens, I still feel fear, but it's not the same bottomless terror. I can see it more clearly and decide what to do. I've made several big decisions since then, like changing careers and moving abroad, that I never would have dared before.
MH04x01: The experience has transformed my mental health. I've had anxiety all my life, and it shaped everything: my choices, my relationships, my career. I always played it safe, and I was always unhappy. Since the experience, my anxiety has decreased dramatically. I'm not saying it's gone, but it doesn't run my life anymore. I've done things I never thought I'd do: I quit my job in accounting and retrained as a landscape gardener, and I moved to Scotland, where I'd always dreamed of living. I'm so much happier now. I feel a deep appreciation for life and for the natural world, which I spend most of my days in now. I'm also more open to new experiences and new people. I've made friends here who are very different from my old friends, and I love that. I feel like I'm finally living my own life.

MH06_01: It hasn't had an impact on how I handle stressful events, I think. I'm about the same. It was more of a spiritual experience for me and didn't touch that area of my life.
MH07_01: It deepened my spirituality and made me feel more connected to something bigger, but I wouldn't say my mental health changed. I was fine before and I'm fine now.

MH06_01: I'm less anxious in stressful situations, mostly because I trust myself more. I know I can handle things.
MH07_01: I'm more confident and less anxious overall. I feel more stable and secure in myself, and I enjoy my life more.

MH06_01: I'm less of a people pleaser now, which has reduced my stress a lot. I say no to things I don't want to do, and I don't feel guilty. During the experience I saw how much I've been bending over backwards for everyone and how exhausted it made me.
MH07_01: I'm less exhausted and resentful, and I like myself more. I understand now that my people pleasing came from wanting to be loved, and that I can love myself without needing everyone's approval.

MH06_01: Ich fühle mich in stressigen Situationen nicht mehr so allein. Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich mir Hilfe holen kann, und mache das jetzt auch.
MH07_01: Ich fühle mich weniger einsam und habe mehr Liebe für meine Freunde und meine Familie. Ich bin offener geworden und lasse Menschen näher an mich heran.

MH06_01: I'm transgender and I came out about a year after the experience. The months around coming out were the most stressful of my life: telling my family, my employer, dealing with the medical system, facing people's reactions. I genuinely don't think I could have done it without the experience. During the trip, I saw myself as I really am, and I felt so much love and acceptance for that person. It was like meeting myself for the first time. That gave me the courage to come out, and it also gave me a kind of inner stability that has helped me through all the stress since. When people misgender me or say hurtful things, it still hurts, but it doesn't shake my sense of who I am. I know who I am now. I've also found a wonderful community of other trans people who support each other, and I lean on them when things get hard. My parents took some time, but they're coming around.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved enormously since the experience and since coming out. Before, I was depressed and anxious most of the time, and I had a constant feeling that something was wrong with me. I didn't know what it was, I just felt like I was living in the wrong life. The experience showed me who I am, and coming out was the beginning of finally living as myself. My depression has lifted almost completely. I still have anxious moments, mostly about how people will treat me, but I feel at home in myself for the first time. I feel so much love, for myself, for my partner, for my trans friends who have become like a family. I'm also more open-minded than I used to be, about gender, about people, about life. I see how many ways there are to be human, and I find that beautiful. I'm grateful every day that I get to live as myself.

MH06_01: I struggled with severe social anxiety for most of my life, and social situations were my biggest source of stress. Job interviews, parties, phone calls, even ordering at a restaurant would make me sweat and shake. During the experience I had an intense feeling of love and connection to other people, all people, and I suddenly saw how much I'd been hiding from them out of fear. I saw that people are mostly kind and that they are as scared as I am. That changed something deep in me. Afterwards I started exposing myself to social situations bit by bit, with the help of a therapist, and it's been so much easier than before. I recently went to a friend's birthday party where I knew almost no one, and I actually enjoyed it. I still get nervous, but it doesn't control my life anymore. Stressful social situations have become manageable, and other kinds of stress feel smaller too, because I'm not constantly exhausted from anxiety.
MH07_01: The experience has been life-changing for my mental health. My social anxiety was so severe that it had led to depression and isolation. I spent most of my twenties alone in my flat, working from home and avoiding people. During the experience I felt a deep love for humanity and a sense that I belong, that I'm part of the human family. It sounds grand, but that's how it felt. Since then, my social anxiety has improved dramatically, with the help of therapy. I have friends now, I go out, I've even started dating. My depression has lifted, because I'm not isolated anymore. I feel so much more open to life, to people, to new experiences. I appreciate every connection I make, because I know how lonely I was before. I'm genuinely happy now, most of the time, which I never thought I'd be able to say.

MH06_01: Ich kann inzwischen besser mit Druck im Job umgehen. Ich arbeite in einer Agentur, und früher hat mich jede Deadline völlig aus der Bahn geworfen. MH07_01: Ich bin insgesamt ausgeglichener und schlafe besser. Ich habe auch wieder mehr Freude an Dingen außerhalb der Arbeit, z.B. am Kochen und an Ausflügen mit meinem Freund. Früher war ich abends nur noch erschöpft und habe mich vor den Fernseher gesetzt. Heute habe ich das Gefühl, wieder ein Leben neben dem Job zu haben, und dafür bin ich sehr dankbar.

MH06_01: I've realised that I can't control other people, and that's taken a lot of stress out of my relationships.
MH07_01: Less frustrated and more at peace in my relationships

MH06_01: Ich habe gelernt, dass ich bei Stress nicht immer sofort eine Lösung finden muss. Manchmal hilft es, einfach abzuwarten und die Situation zu beobachten. Früher habe ich in Panik irgendetwas getan, nur um das Gefühl der Hilflosigkeit loszuwerden. Heute kann ich die Unsicherheit besser aushalten.
MH07_01: Ich bin weniger ängstlich und kann Unsicherheit besser aushalten. Dadurch bin ich psychisch stabiler geworden und habe weniger Panikattacken. Ich fühle mich insgesamt sicherer in meinem Leben.

MH06_01: Kurz nach der Erfahrung hat sich mein Partner von mir getrennt, nach neun Jahren. Das war ein riesiger Schock. Ich glaube, dass ich ohne die Erfahrung viel schlechter damit umgegangen wäre. Das hat mir geholfen, die Trennung als einen schmerzhaften, aber vorübergehenden Abschnitt zu sehen. Ich habe mir erlaubt, traurig zu sein, ohne mich darin zu verlieren.
MH07_01: Ich fühle mich offener und liebevoller, gegenüber mir selbst und anderen Menschen. Ich habe neue Menschen kennengelernt und mich auf neue Erfahrungen eingelassen, z.B. habe ich einen Kletterkurs angefangen und bin allein nach Portugal gereist. Ich bin offener für das, was das Leben bringt, und habe weniger Angst vor Veränderungen. Insgesamt würde ich sagen, dass es mir psychisch so gut geht wie lange nicht.

MH06_01: Calmer under pressure. I handled my wedding planning without a single meltdown, which my mum says is a miracle.
MH07_01: I'm happier and less anxious in general. I enjoy things more and I'm not as tense.

MH05x01: Probleme erscheinen mir kleiner, weil ich mich als Teil von etwas Größerem fühle.
MH04x01: Ich fühle mich mit allem verbunden und weniger einsam. Das gibt mir viel Kraft und Liebe.

MH06_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir geholfen, belastende Lebensereignisse in einem größeren Zusammenhang zu sehen. Ich bin religiös erzogen worden, habe mich aber schon lange vom Glauben entfernt. Wenn heute etwas Schlimmes passiert, wie die Krankheit meiner Mutter oder die Arbeitslosigkeit meines Mannes, dann gerate ich zwar auch in Sorge, aber ich habe dieses Grundvertrauen, dass wir das durchstehen werden und dass auch schwierige Zeiten einen Sinn haben können. Ich bete sogar manchmal wieder, auf meine eigene Art.
MH07_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir ein tiefes Gefühl von Geborgenheit gegeben, das ich vorher nicht kannte. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine unglaubliche Liebe gespürt, die mich umgeben hat, und das Gefühl, dass ich nie wirklich allein bin. MH06_01: I have borderline personality disorder and I've been doing DBT for some years. The experience made the skills from DBT make sense on a deeper level. MH07_01: My BPD symptoms are less intense since the experience. I have fewer emotional crises and I don't self harm anymore. I feel more stable and I can regulate my emotions better, which also helps my relationships.

MH06_01: I've been dealing with OCD and anxiety since I was a teenager, and stressful events always made my symptoms much worse. I also started doing ERP therapy after the experience, which I'd been avoiding for years. Now when something stressful happens, I notice the urge to check or count, and I can name it and sit with the discomfort for a while instead of giving in. It's not perfect but I'm handling stress much better.
MH07_01: My OCD and anxiety have both improved a lot. I would say the experience opened a door, and then the therapy helped me walk through it. My compulsions take up maybe an hour a day now, compared to several hours before, and my anxiety is much more manageable. I also understand myself much better. I used to think my OCD was a character flaw, but now I see it as my brain trying to keep me safe in a world that felt very unsafe when I was a kid. That understanding has made me much kinder to myself. I have more energy for things I enjoy, and I've started dating again, which I hadn't done in years because I was so ashamed of my symptoms.

MH07_01: Ich habe alte Verletzungen verarbeiten können und bin dadurch innerlich ruhiger geworden. Ich habe weniger Albträume und fühle mich sicherer. Ich verstehe besser, warum ich so empfindlich auf Kritik reagiert habe.

MH07_01: A bit happier

MH07_01: Less anxious, more balanced. Better at controlling my emotions.

MH06_01: Leider eher negativ. Nach der Erfahrung, die sehr beängstigend war, war ich über Monate hinweg viel stressanfälliger als vorher. Kleinigkeiten, wie ein voller Bus oder ein lautes Geräusch, haben bei mir Herzrasen und Panik ausgelöst. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Nervensystem überreizt ist. Ich habe dann mit einer Therapie begonnen, und es ist besser geworden, aber ich bin immer noch empfindlicher, wenn es stressig wird. Ich glaube, ich war damals einfach nicht in der richtigen Verfassung für so eine starke Erfahrung, und das hat Spuren hinterlassen.
MH07_01: Die Erfahrung hat sich negativ auf meine psychische Gesundheit ausgewirkt. Ich hatte danach mehrere Monate lang Angstzustände, Schlafstörungen und das Gefühl, nicht ganz in der Realität zu sein. Ich hatte große Angst, dass ich psychotisch werde. Mit Hilfe einer Therapeutin habe ich gelernt, damit umzugehen, und heute geht es mir wieder deutlich besser, aber ganz verschwunden sind die Ängste nicht.

MH06_01: The experience completely changed my relationship to stress, and I think it's because of what happened with my body during the trip. I'd been suffering from chronic tension headaches and jaw pain for years, which my doctor said was stress-related. During the experience, I became aware of how much I was clenching my jaw and tensing my neck and shoulders, and when I let go, it was like a dam breaking. I shook and cried for maybe twenty minutes, and then I felt a lightness I hadn't felt since childhood. That experience made me realise that my body had been holding all my stress for me. Since then I pay a lot of attention to my body when I'm stressed. I check in a few times a day: am I clenching? Are my shoulders up? I've also started going to a Feldenkrais class and I do progressive muscle relaxation before sleep. My headaches have reduced by about 80 percent, and I deal with stressful events much better because I'm not starting from a place of constant tension.
MH07_01: The experience has improved both my physical and mental health. My headaches and jaw pain have decreased dramatically, and I think that's had a knock-on effect on my mood. Chronic pain is exhausting, and I hadn't realised how much it was dragging me down. I'm much less irritable and much happier now. I also feel a deep appreciation for my body, which I used to just ignore. I understand now that my body was carrying my stress for me, and I'm grateful to it. I've become much more open to things like bodywork and somatic therapy, which I would have dismissed as woo-woo before. My mental health is probably the best it's been in a decade.

MH06_01: I'm a much calmer parent. My son has autism and meltdowns used to make me panic and shout. Now I can stay calm and be there for him. I learned during the experience to stay present in chaos.
MH07_01: I'm less anxious and depressed. Being a calmer parent has made me happier too, and I appreciate my son for who he is now instead of wishing he were different. I see so much beauty in him that I couldn't see before because I was always stressed.

MH06_01: Mehr Ruhe, weniger Hektik
MH07_01: Ich bin ausgeglichener

When my relationship was going through a rough patch last year, I suggested we go to couples therapy instead of hiding at the office. It was uncomfortable, but it helped.
MH07_01: I'm more emotionally honest and less avoidant, which has improved my mental health. I used to have a lot of hidden anxiety that I numbed with work. Now that I face things, I feel more grounded and less on edge. I understand myself better and I'm working on things in therapy. My relationship is also better, which makes me happier.

MH06_01: Ich gehe mit Stress heute anders um, weil ich gelernt habe, auf meine Gefühle zu achten, statt sie zu ignorieren. In der Erfahrung habe ich gemerkt, wie viel Angst und Traurigkeit ich mit mir herumtrage, ohne es zu wissen. Ich hatte immer gedacht, ich sei einfach ein rationaler Mensch, der sich nicht so von Gefühlen beeinflussen lässt. Das war ein Irrtum. Seit der Erfahrung nehme ich mir Zeit, in mich hineinzuhören, wenn ich gestresst bin. Ich frage mich, was ich gerade fühle und was ich brauche. Ich bin weniger erschöpft und treffe bessere Entscheidungen, weil ich nicht mehr gegen mich selbst arbeite.
MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung deutlich verbessert, auch wenn das zunächst nicht so aussah. Ich bin auch offener geworden für Dinge, die ich früher als esoterisch abgetan hätte, wie Meditation oder Körperarbeit. Das hat mein Leben sehr bereichert.

MH06_01: The biggest change for me is that I don't isolate myself anymore when things get hard. I used to go silent for days and not tell anyone what was going on. Now I reach out. MH07_01: I feel more loved and connected than I ever have. During the experience I had this sense of being held by everyone I love, and it made me cry for an hour. MH06_01: I'm a single father of two and I work shifts in a warehouse, so stress has been my normal state for years. I didn't go into the experience expecting much, a friend just offered and I was curious. But it ended up changing how I see my life. During the trip I sat in my friend's garden for hours watching the light change, and I had this overwhelming feeling that I'm doing okay. Not perfect, but okay. My kids are fed and loved, I show up for work, I keep going. I'd never once given myself credit for that. Since then, when things get on top of me, like when the car breaks down or the kids are sick and I can't take time off, I try to remember that feeling. I tell myself I'm doing my best and that's enough. It sounds small but it's changed how stressed I feel. I'm less hard on myself, less angry, and I've started asking my mum and my neighbour for help more, which I used to be too proud to do.
MH07_01: I think my mental health is better than it's been since my kids were born. I didn't realise how depressed I was until I started to come out of it. I used to feel like I was failing at everything and that I'd never have a moment for myself. The experience gave me a feeling of being okay, of being enough, and that has slowly changed how I feel day to day. I appreciate my kids so much more now, instead of just seeing them as another job. We have pancake Saturdays and we go to the park, and I actually enjoy it instead of counting the minutes. I'm also kinder to myself, which has made me less irritable. I still get tired, of course, but I don't feel that heavy hopelessness anymore. I feel a lot of love for my kids and for my mum, who helps us so much, and I tell them more often.

MH06_01: Ich habe durch die Erfahrung einen anderen Blick auf meine Arbeit bekommen. Ich bin Projektleiterin in einem großen Unternehmen und war früher ständig unter Strom. Jede Verzögerung, jeder Fehler eines Teammitglieds hat mich persönlich getroffen. In der Erfahrung habe ich gesehen, wie sehr ich mich über meinen Job definiere und wie wenig das eigentlich mit mir als Mensch zu tun hat. Seitdem kann ich Probleme im Job mit mehr Abstand betrachten. Ich bin immer noch engagiert, aber ich nehme es nicht mehr so persönlich.
MH07_01: Ich bin ausgeglichener und habe weniger Stresssymptome wie Schlafprobleme und Magenschmerzen. Ich habe auch mehr Freude an meinem Leben außerhalb der Arbeit und nehme mir mehr Zeit für Freunde und Hobbys. Ich verstehe jetzt besser, warum ich mich so über meinen Job definiert habe, und das hilft mir, mich davon zu lösen.

MH06_01: The experience showed me where a lot of my stress reactions come from. When someone raises their voice I freeze, and during the trip I went back to being 7 years old and hiding under the table while my parents fought. I saw that the freeze is that little kid trying to protect himself. Since then, when I get into a stressful situation, especially conflicts, I can sometimes recognise that it's the old reaction and not the actual situation. I tell myself, you're not 7 anymore, you can speak. It doesn't make the stress go away but I understand it, and I'm less ashamed of it. I also told my partner about this so she understands why I go quiet.
MH07_01: It has improved my mental health in the sense that I understand myself better. I've had depression on and off since my teens and always felt it was just something wrong with me. After the experience, I see it more as a response to what I went through as a kid. That has made me kinder to myself. I'm still in therapy, and the experience gave me a lot of material to work with. My depressive episodes have become shorter and less intense, I think because I don't add self-hatred on top of the sadness anymore. I'm not cured, but I'm in a much better place.

MH06_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir geholfen, eine sehr schwierige Phase in meinem Leben zu bewältigen. Ich war damals arbeitslos, frisch getrennt und hatte große Geldsorgen. Ich fühlte mich als Versager und hatte manchmal Gedanken, dass es besser wäre, nicht mehr da zu sein. Ein Freund hat mich zu einer begleiteten Zeremonie mitgenommen. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, dass mein Leben wertvoll ist, unabhängig davon, ob ich einen Job habe oder in einer Beziehung bin. Ich habe auch gespürt, wie sehr mich meine Freunde und meine Familie lieben. Das hat mir neuen Mut gegeben. In den Monaten danach habe ich mir Hilfe gesucht, eine Therapie angefangen und mich bei verschiedenen Stellen beworben. Heute habe ich wieder einen Job und eine neue Partnerin. Wenn ich heute in eine schwierige Situation komme, erinnere ich mich an das Gefühl, dass mein Leben wertvoll ist, und dass ich nicht allein bin. Das hilft mir, nicht in Verzweiflung zu verfallen.
MH07_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir in einer Zeit, in der es mir sehr schlecht ging, das Leben gerettet, so dramatisch das auch klingt. Ich hatte damals Suizidgedanken und war in einer tiefen Depression. Ich habe mich wertlos und allein gefühlt. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine Liebe gespürt, die alles verändert hat. Ich habe gespürt, dass ich geliebt werde, von meinen Freunden, von meiner Familie und von etwas Größerem, das ich nicht benennen kann. Ich habe gespürt, dass mein Leben einen Wert hat. Nach der Erfahrung habe ich mir professionelle Hilfe gesucht und eine Therapie begonnen. Die Depression hat sich langsam gebessert, und heute geht es mir gut. Ich bin dankbar für jeden Tag und für die Menschen, die mich durch diese Zeit begleitet haben. Ich bin auch offener geworden, für neue Menschen und neue Erfahrungen, und ich habe das Gefühl, dass mein Leben heute reicher ist als vor der Krise.

MH06_01: I'm more forgiving when people let me down, which reduces stress in my relationships a lot.
MH07_01: I feel more love and less resentment towards people. Happier overall.

MH06_01: The experience took place during a very difficult time in my life. I had just found out that my husband had been cheating on me for two years, and I was devastated. I took mushrooms with a close friend who has experience with them, mainly because I wanted to feel something other than pain. What happened was not what I expected. I spent the first part of the trip in deep grief, sobbing on the floor. But then I felt a kind of strength rising in me, a sense that I would survive this and that I deserved better. I also saw my own part in the marriage, how I had made myself small and ignored my own needs for years. That was hard to see but also freeing. Since then, I've dealt with the divorce, moving house, and becoming a single mother, and I've handled it all with a strength I didn't know I had. I still have bad days, but I don't feel like a victim anymore.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot, considering everything I've been through. The experience gave me a sense of self-worth that I had lost during my marriage. I realised that I deserve to be loved and respected, and that I can love myself even if no one else does. That has been the foundation of my recovery. I've been in therapy, which has helped me process the betrayal and the grief, and I've started to rebuild my life. I'm more open to new experiences, I travel with my daughter, I've taken up painting, and I've made new friends. I feel stronger and more independent than ever. I'm also much more aware of my own patterns in relationships, which I think will help me in the future. I'm not ready to date yet, but I'm hopeful.

MH06_01: Ich bin seitdem gelassener und kann mit Unsicherheit besser leben. Das hat mir vor allem bei der Jobsuche nach dem Studium geholfen, die sich sehr lange hingezogen hat. Ich habe darauf vertraut, dass es irgendwann klappt.
MH07_01: Ich bin optimistischer geworden und habe weniger Zukunftsängste. Ich glaube daran, dass sich die Dinge fügen werden, und das gibt mir Ruhe. Ich bin auch dankbarer für das, was ich habe, auch wenn noch nicht alles so ist, wie ich es mir wünsche.

MH06_01: Before the experience I would always react to stress with anger. I would yell at my partner, slam doors, sometimes punch walls. I hated myself for it afterwards. During the experience I saw my anger very clearly, as a kind of shield. Underneath it was fear, fear of not being good enough, of being abandoned. Seeing this has changed how I handle stressful situations. When I feel the anger coming up now, I try to stop and ask myself what I'm afraid of. Often I can then talk about the fear instead of exploding. I've also started therapy to work on this, and I use some techniques from there, like counting to ten and leaving the room for a few minutes. My partner says I'm much easier to live with. I still mess up sometimes but it's maybe 20% of what it used to be.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot. I used to have anxiety and anger issues, and I was always on edge. Since the experience my anxiety is much lower, I'd say I went from a 7 out of 10 to a 3 out of 10 on most days. I understand where my anger comes from, which has made it less scary and easier to manage. I think the biggest change is that I'm not ashamed of myself anymore. I used to think I was a bad person because of my temper, now I see that I was a scared kid who learned to protect himself. With that understanding, I can have compassion for myself, and that has helped more than anything else. I've also started seeing a therapist, which I never would have done before, because I didn't think I deserved help. My relationship has improved and I feel more connected to my partner and my friends. Overall I would say I'm healthier and happier than I've been in my adult life.

MH06_01: I've lived with chronic back pain for eight years, and the pain itself is one of the most stressful things in my life, along with everything that comes with it: missed work, doctor appointments, people not believing me. The experience happened at a retreat where I went specifically to work on my relationship to the pain. During the ceremony I could feel the pain, but it was just a sensation, it wasn't attached to all the fear and anger. Since then, when I have a bad pain day, I can sometimes remember that and not add the extra layer of panic. I've also become better at saying no to things when I'm in pain, without feeling guilty.
MH07_01: Living with chronic pain had made me quite depressed, I felt my life was over at 35. The experience didn't take the pain away, but it took away a lot of the despair. I'm much less depressed now and I've found ways to enjoy life within my limits, like painting and gardening, which I can do even on bad days. I feel grateful for what my body can still do instead of only angry about what it can't. My psychiatrist reduced my antidepressants because I'm doing so much better.

Seitdem merke ich, dass ich Dinge nicht mehr so leicht wegschieben kann, und das ist gut so. Ich setze mich heute mit belastenden Situationen auseinander, rede darüber und lasse meine Gefühle zu. Das ist anstrengender als Verdrängen, aber auf lange Sicht viel gesünder. Ich fühle mich heute stabiler als früher, auch wenn ich manchmal mehr fühle, als mir lieb ist.
MH07_01: Ich bin heute psychisch stabiler, obwohl ich mehr fühle als früher. Das klingt vielleicht widersprüchlich, aber ich glaube, das Verdrängen hat mich auf Dauer viel mehr Kraft gekostet. MH07_01: Ich bin dankbarer für mein Leben und genieße die Momente mehr. Ich habe auch das Gefühl, dass ich mehr Freude an meiner Arbeit und an meinen Hobbys habe.

MH07_01: My mental health has improved because I'm no longer carrying my parents' problems. I used to feel responsible for their happiness, which made me anxious and depressed. Now I see that I can love them without fixing them. I feel lighter and more free, and I have more energy for my own life. I've also become more compassionate towards both of them, which has made our relationships better even though they're struggling.

I'm in my early thirties and all my friends seem to be getting married, buying houses, having kids, and I'm still renting and single. I used to feel like a failure every time someone posted an engagement photo. During the experience I felt completely content with my own life, exactly as it is. Since then, I've noticed when I'm comparing and I try to let it go. I've also stopped following a lot of accounts that made me feel bad.
MH07_01: I'm more content with my life and less anxious about where I'm supposed to be by now. I appreciate what I have: good friends, a job I mostly like, my health, my little flat. MH06_01: This is a difficult question because I think the experience changed many things at once. The most important thing for handling stress is that I understand myself a lot better. I grew up in a household with a lot of chaos, my dad drank and my mom was depressed, and I learned very early to be hypervigilant, to read the room, to take care of everyone. When I'm under stress, I go into that mode automatically: I try to control everything, I don't sleep, I work all the time and I don't ask for help. During the experience, I saw this pattern so clearly, like a film of my life, and I saw how much it has cost me. I also saw that I don't need to do this anymore, that I'm safe now. Since then I notice when I'm going into control mode and I try to stop, take a breath and ask myself what I actually need. Sometimes it's just rest. I've also started to set more boundaries with my family, which has reduced a lot of my stress. It's an ongoing process but I'm much better at it than before.
MH07_01: I would say the experience improved my mental health quite significantly, but not in a magical way. It gave me a deep understanding of why I am the way I am, which I couldn't get from years of talking therapy. Knowing that my hypervigilance, my control issues and my exhaustion are all connected to my childhood has helped me to let go of the idea that I'm just weak or broken. Since then I've had fewer burnout episodes and my mood is more stable. I sleep better because I'm not constantly on alert. I've also become more compassionate with myself and others. I still have bad days, but I can recognise them for what they are and I don't panic. Something I didn't expect: I started to feel much more connected to people, I have more empathy for my parents and I've reconnected with my brother, who I hadn't talked to in years. I feel like I have a better foundation now. My therapist says the change has been remarkable and I agree, though I think a lot of the work happened after the experience, in integrating it.

MH06_01: The experience made me realise I had been dissociating for years as a way to cope with stress. When things got hard, I'd go into a kind of fog where nothing felt real. During the experience I felt more present in my body than I had in a very long time, and I could see the contrast. Since then I've been working with a therapist to stay present when I'm stressed. It's hard, but I'm much better at it than I was.
MH07_01: I'm more present and less dissociated. I feel more alive, which is sometimes overwhelming but mostly good. My anxiety and depression are better, and I understand myself and my coping mechanisms much better than before.
