MH06_01: I had been dealing with a lot of stress around my immigration status. I've lived in this country for 12 years, but my visa situation has always been uncertain, and every renewal was a nightmare that kept me up for weeks. During the experience I had a sense that my home is not a place or a piece of paper, but something inside me. That has helped me a lot. The last renewal was stressful, but I didn't lose sleep over it. I did what I needed to do and trusted that I would be okay, wherever I ended up. I also talked to other people in the same situation, which made me feel less alone.
MH07_01: I feel more at peace and at home in myself. My anxiety, which was always connected to the visa situation and the feeling of not belonging, has gone down a lot. I'm also more open to connecting with people here. I used to keep to myself because I thought I might have to leave anyway. Now I've made real friends and I feel part of a community. I'm grateful for my life here, whatever happens in the future, and I feel a lot of love for the people I've met.

MH06_01: I'm less afraid of conflict. I used to avoid it at all costs, but now I can have a difficult conversation with my boss or my roommate without my heart pounding for hours. I think the experience made me feel more solid in myself.
MH07_01: I feel more confident and self-assured, and less anxious. I'm more open to meeting new people too.

MH06_01: Ich bin seit der Erfahrung gelassener, wenn es Konflikte gibt, und kann meine Meinung ruhiger vertreten. Früher habe ich entweder geschwiegen oder bin laut geworden. Jetzt finde ich öfter einen Mittelweg.
MH07_01: Ich fühle mich selbstbewusster und psychisch stabiler. Ich habe gelernt, für mich einzustehen, und das hat meine Stimmung und mein Selbstwertgefühl verbessert. Ich bin auch offener anderen Meinungen gegenüber, weil ich mich nicht mehr so schnell angegriffen fühle.

MH06_01: I'm more relaxed in general and less likely to get stressed about small things
MH07_01: Things don't matter as much to me as they used to. I just shrug.

MH05x01: My life has been quite stressful in the last couple of years, I lost my job, my mother died, and I moved to a new city. Before the experience, I think I would have fallen apart, because I always tried to handle everything alone and pretend I was fine. The experience taught me two things. First, that it's okay to feel what I feel, and that sadness and fear are not enemies. I let myself cry when my mother died, a lot, and I didn't feel ashamed. Second, that I'm not alone. During the experience I felt deeply connected to my friends and family, and I realised that they want to be there for me. So when things got hard, I asked for help. My best friend came to stay with me for a week after the funeral. My sister and I talked on the phone every day. I joined a grief group in my new city. I'm still sad sometimes, of course, but I feel I've dealt with all of this in a much healthier way than I ever could have before. I'm proud of how I handled it, which I never would have said about myself before.
MH04x01: The experience helped my mental health in many ways. Before, I was quite depressed and lonely, though I didn't really admit it to myself. I was working all the time and I had few close relationships. During the experience, I felt this overwhelming love, first from my mother, who was still alive then, and then from everyone in my life, and then from something bigger. I can't describe it properly. It was like being bathed in warm light. I came back from it crying with gratitude. Since then, my depression has lifted, slowly but steadily. I've reconnected with old friends and made new ones. I let people in. When my mother died, I was devastated, but I also felt that her love was still with me, which comforted me a lot. I'm a much more open, loving and happy person now. I still have hard days, but I don't feel the emptiness I used to feel. I would say this experience was one of the most important things that has ever happened to me.

MH06_01: I'm less overwhelmed by the news and world events. I used to doomscroll and get really anxious about climate change and politics. The experience gave me some perspective, and now I limit my news intake and focus on what I can do locally. I volunteer at a community garden, which helps me feel like I'm contributing instead of just worrying.
MH07_01: I'm less anxious and less depressed about the state of the world. I still care, but I don't feel hopeless anymore. I'm more grateful for the people around me and for the small things that make life good. The community garden has been great for me, I've met a lot of lovely people.

MH06_01: I'm less reactive and more patient with myself and with others. Small problems don't get to me anymore.
MH07_01: I'm more patient, calmer and generally happier. I feel more at peace.

MH06_01: I deal with stressful events much better now. The biggest change is in my relationship with uncertainty. I used to need to know what was coming, and the not knowing was what stressed me out the most. During the experience, I completely lost my sense of time and space, I didn't know where I was or who I was for a while, and it was terrifying at first. But then I relaxed into it and it was beautiful. I learned that I can survive not knowing. That has helped me with everything from waiting for medical results to job applications to my partner's long trips abroad. I still feel the uncertainty, but it doesn't eat me alive anymore.
MH07_01: I'm much less anxious than I used to be. I had generalized anxiety for years, and I was always worried about something, my health, my partner, my job. Learning to tolerate uncertainty has been the key for me. I'm more relaxed, I sleep better and I'm happier. I'm also more open to new experiences, because I'm not so afraid of the unknown. I've started traveling more, which I used to avoid because it felt too unpredictable.

MH06_01: I'm a police officer, and I've seen a lot of terrible things. I had been struggling with intrusive images and irritability for years. The experience was part of a retreat for first responders. What it gave me was a sense of compassion for myself and for the people I meet on the job, including the ones who do bad things. I saw that most of them are hurting too. That has changed how I handle stressful calls. I'm calmer, less reactive, and I don't carry so much anger home with me. I also talk to my colleagues about what we see, which we never used to do. We've started a small peer group.
MH07_01: My PTSD symptoms have gotten better. I have fewer intrusive images, I sleep better, and I'm not as irritable. But the biggest thing is that I feel more love and compassion, for myself and for others. I'd become really cynical and hard after years on the job, and the experience softened that. My wife says she has her husband back. I'm also more open to talking about mental health, which is still a bit of a taboo in my line of work. I've encouraged a few colleagues to get help.

MH06_01: I've learned to just let things be sometimes. I used to have to fix every problem right away, and now I can leave things for a while and come back to them when I'm calmer.
MH07_01: I'm less anxious and more relaxed. I don't feel the constant urge to fix everything.

MH05x01: I'm less afraid of my own emotions, so stressful events don't feel as overwhelming. I know I can feel sad or angry or scared and still be okay.
MH04x01: I'm less afraid of my emotions and that has helped my anxiety and depression. I feel more whole.

MH06_01: I'm better at handling the stress of parenting. My kids are 3 and 5 and it's chaos. I used to lose my temper a lot. Now I can usually take a breath and respond calmly. I also accept that some days will just be hard, and that's ok.
MH07_01: I'm a happier and more relaxed parent. I enjoy my kids so much more now, instead of just trying to get through the day. I feel so much love for them and I'm less hard on myself when I make mistakes.

MH06_01: Seit der Erfahrung bin ich gelassener im Umgang mit meinen Kindern. Ich habe zwei Teenager, und es gibt oft Streit. Früher habe ich mich sehr schnell aufgeregt und bin laut geworden. Heute kann ich eher durchatmen und versuchen zu verstehen, was in ihnen vorgeht. Ich erinnere mich daran, wie ich selbst in dem Alter war. Das hilft mir, ruhig zu bleiben.
MH07_01: Ich bin psychisch ausgeglichener und streite weniger mit meinen Kindern. Das hat die Stimmung in unserer Familie sehr verbessert. Ich fühle mich wohler und habe mehr Freude am Familienleben. Ich bin dankbar für meine Kinder, auch wenn sie mich manchmal in den Wahnsinn treiben.

MH06_01: Ich habe gelernt, Hilfe anzunehmen. Früher dachte ich, ich müsse alles allein schaffen. Jetzt frage ich Freunde oder Familie, wenn ich Unterstützung brauche, und das macht vieles leichter.
MH07_01: Ich fühle mich weniger allein und mehr unterstützt. Das hat meine Stimmung sehr verbessert, und ich habe weniger depressive Phasen.

MH06_01: Ich habe die Erfahrung in einer Zeit gemacht, in der ich mit einer schweren Erschöpfungsdepression zu kämpfen hatte. Ich war seit Monaten krankgeschrieben und hatte das Gefühl, dass ich nie wieder arbeiten kann. Jede kleine Belastung, wie ein Telefonat mit der Krankenkasse oder ein Arzttermin, hat mich völlig überfordert. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, wie viel Kraft eigentlich noch in mir steckt, nur verschüttet unter Erschöpfung und Selbstzweifeln. Ich habe auch gesehen, wie sehr ich mich über Jahre hinweg überfordert habe, weil ich niemanden enttäuschen wollte. Diese Erkenntnis war schmerzhaft, aber auch befreiend. In den Monaten danach habe ich mit meiner Therapeutin daran gearbeitet, meine Grenzen besser wahrzunehmen. Heute arbeite ich wieder, allerdings in Teilzeit, und ich gehe mit Stress viel achtsamer um. Ich merke früher, wenn es zu viel wird, und kann dann rechtzeitig gegensteuern, z.B. indem ich mir einen freien Tag nehme oder Aufgaben abgebe.
MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich nach der Erfahrung langsam, aber stetig verbessert. Ich litt damals an einer schweren Erschöpfungsdepression und hatte das Gefühl, nie wieder gesund zu werden. Die Erfahrung hat mir einen Hoffnungsschimmer gegeben. Ich habe gespürt, dass in mir noch Lebensfreude und Kraft stecken, und ich habe verstanden, warum ich mich so lange überfordert habe. Mit Hilfe meiner Therapeutin habe ich an diesen Erkenntnissen weitergearbeitet. Heute geht es mir deutlich besser. Ich habe wieder Freude an Dingen, die mir früher wichtig waren, wie Gartenarbeit und Musik. Ich schlafe besser und habe mehr Energie. Vor allem habe ich gelernt, besser für mich zu sorgen, und ich weiß jetzt, dass ich nicht immer funktionieren muss. Ich bin dankbar für jeden guten Tag, und ich nehme die schönen Momente viel bewusster wahr als früher.

MH06_01: I've realised that I'm a highly sensitive person and that a lot of my stress comes from overstimulation. During the experience everything was so intense, sounds, lights, emotions, and I suddenly understood that this is a heightened version of how I experience the world every day. That was a revelation. Since then I've been much better at managing my energy. I wear earplugs in loud places, I take breaks from social events, I don't schedule too much in one day. I don't feel guilty about it anymore. This has made a huge difference, I'm less exhausted and I can handle stressful events much better when I'm not already overstimulated.
MH07_01: Understanding that I'm highly sensitive has been life-changing for my mental health. I used to think something was wrong with me because I got overwhelmed so easily. I had burnouts twice. Now I know how I work, and I can plan my life accordingly. I'm less exhausted, less anxious and I have more energy for things I enjoy. I also have more self-acceptance. I used to try to be like everyone else, and now I accept that I'm different, and that it's okay. I've even started to see my sensitivity as a strength, because it lets me feel things deeply, like music and art and nature, and I appreciate those things so much more now.

MH06_01: I'm better at stopping my anxiety from spiralling. I used to have one anxious thought and then twenty more would follow, until I was in a full panic. During the experience I watched my thoughts like a chain reaction and saw how each one triggered the next. Since then I try to catch the first one and gently set it aside. I also use a breathing technique I learned in the integration sessions afterwards.
MH07_01: My anxiety has improved a lot. I still have anxious thoughts, but they don't take over like they used to. I feel more in control and more confident. I'm also more open to doing things I used to avoid because of anxiety, like travelling and meeting new people.

MH06_01: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, ob sich etwas verändert hat. Ich glaube eher nicht.
MH07_01: Kein Einfluss, soweit ich das sagen kann.

MH06_01: Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich in stressigen Zeiten oft unfair zu meinem Partner werde, weil ich meinen Frust an ihm auslasse. Seit der Erfahrung achte ich mehr darauf und entschuldige mich, wenn es doch passiert. Wir reden mehr darüber, was uns belastet.
MH07_01: Ich bin weniger gereizt und kann mich besser selbst regulieren. Unsere Beziehung ist dadurch harmonischer geworden, und ich fühle mich glücklicher und ausgeglichener.

MH06_01: I'm a single mum of three and stress is basically my life. The experience didn't change my circumstances but it changed my attitude a lot. I stopped trying to be the perfect mum and I let things be messy. I laugh more with my kids, and when it's chaos I just breathe and remind myself that this phase won't last forever. I also started asking my neighbour for help sometimes, which I was too proud to do before.
MH07_01: I'm happier and more relaxed with my kids. I enjoy being a mum more, instead of just surviving. I appreciate the little moments, like bedtime stories or when they make me a drawing. I also feel less guilty all the time, which has improved my mood a lot.

MH06_01: About the same as before, I'd say. Maybe I'm a bit more relaxed but I'm not sure it's because of the experience.
MH07_01: Hard to say, I don't think it changed much. Maybe a little more relaxed.

MH06_01: I've started doing breathwork and cold showers since the experience. When I feel stressed I do box breathing for a few minutes. Helps me a lot.
MH07_01: I felt fantastic for maybe a month after, then it faded. I'm about where I was before, maybe slightly better.

MH06_01: Ich habe die Erfahrung gemacht, als ich mitten in einer Krise steckte. Ich war Anfang dreißig, hatte gerade mein Studium abgebrochen, war von meinem Freund verlassen worden und hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Leben ein einziges Scheitern ist. Ich hatte Angst vor jeder Entscheidung und habe mich wochenlang in meiner Wohnung verkrochen. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine unglaubliche Weite erlebt, als würde ich über einer Landschaft schweben und mein ganzes Leben von oben sehen. Ich habe gesehen, dass mein Leben noch lang ist, dass es viele Wege gibt und dass ich nicht gescheitert bin, sondern einfach an einer Kreuzung stehe. Das hat mir unglaublich viel Mut gegeben. In den Monaten danach habe ich eine Ausbildung zur Ergotherapeutin angefangen, die mir sehr viel Freude macht. Ich habe auch gelernt, mit schwierigen Situationen anders umzugehen. Ich sehe sie heute eher als Teil einer größeren Reise und nicht mehr als Beweis dafür, dass ich nichts tauge.
MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung grundlegend verbessert. Ich war damals in einer tiefen Krise, hatte depressive Symptome und fühlte mich wertlos und gescheitert. Ich konnte mich über nichts mehr freuen und hatte kaum noch Hoffnung. Die Erfahrung hat mir gezeigt, dass mein Leben noch viele Möglichkeiten bereithält und dass ich nicht gescheitert bin. Das hat mir neuen Mut gegeben. Heute geht es mir gut. Ich habe eine Ausbildung gefunden, die mich erfüllt, und neue Freunde, die mich unterstützen. Ich bin offener geworden für neue Erfahrungen und habe weniger Angst vor Veränderungen. Vor allem aber bin ich dankbar für mein Leben, für jeden Tag, für die kleinen Freuden. Ich nehme die Welt bewusster wahr und kann mich wieder an Dingen erfreuen, die ich früher übersehen habe, wie einem Sonnenuntergang oder einem guten Gespräch.

MH06_01: After the experience I started meditating every morning for 10-15 minutes. When something stressful happens I use the breathing technique from my practice, and I go for a run if I can. These habits help me deal with stress much better than before.
MH07_01: For about two weeks after the experience I felt amazing, light and happy and full of energy. Then slowly it went back to normal, and now I'd say I'm about the same as before. Meditation helps a bit to keep some of it.

MH06_01: I used to deal with stress by shopping. Whenever I felt anxious or overwhelmed, I'd buy things online, and I got into quite a lot of debt. During the experience, I saw this pattern very clearly and I saw the emptiness I was trying to fill. It was not a nice thing to see. Since then I've been working on it. I've deleted my shopping apps, I've talked to a debt counsellor, and when I feel the urge to buy something, I try to sit with the feeling instead. I've also started going for walks when I'm stressed. It's been hard, but I'm slowly getting out of debt and I feel more in control.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved since I started dealing with my shopping addiction. I used to be anxious and ashamed all the time because of my debt, and I'd hide bills from my partner. Now I'm more honest and I feel much lighter. I also understand myself much better. I see that I was trying to fill an emptiness that came from feeling unloved as a child. That understanding has helped me be more compassionate with myself.

MH06_01: I'm much better at letting things go. When something bad happens, I deal with it and then I don't keep thinking about it for days.
MH07_01: I'm lighter and less anxious. I don't ruminate like I used to.

MH06_01: Honestly it made it worse. The experience was a bad trip and for months afterwards any stress at all would trigger a feeling of panic and unreality, like I was back in it. I avoided crowded places and stressful conversations. It's better now, two years later, but I'm still more sensitive to stress than I was before.
MH07_01: Negatively. After the experience I had derealisation for months, the world felt fake and I was scared I had damaged my brain. I also had a lot of anxiety and couldn't concentrate at university. It has slowly gotten better, with the help of a therapist, but I'm still not completely back to how I was before the trip.

MH06_01: Die Erfahrung hat mir geholfen, eine schwierige Lebensphase zu überstehen. Ich war damals mitten in einer Scheidung, hatte einen Rechtsstreit mit meinem Ex-Mann um das Sorgerecht und wusste nicht, wie ich das alles finanziell schaffen sollte. Ich hatte ständig Angst und konnte kaum schlafen. Eine Freundin, die Erfahrung mit Psilocybin hatte, hat mich begleitet. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, dass ich stark bin und dass ich meinen Kindern eine gute Mutter sein kann, egal was passiert. Ich habe auch gesehen, dass mein Ex-Mann selbst voller Angst ist, und konnte ein wenig Mitgefühl für ihn entwickeln. Das hat die Verhandlungen erstaunlicherweise einfacher gemacht, weil ich nicht mehr so wütend war. Wir haben uns schließlich außergerichtlich geeinigt. Ich habe in dieser Zeit auch gelernt, Hilfe anzunehmen, von meinen Eltern, von Freundinnen, von einer Beratungsstelle. Heute bin ich stolz darauf, wie ich diese Zeit gemeistert habe.
MH07_01: Ich bin psychisch stabiler und selbstbewusster geworden. In der Zeit der Scheidung war ich sehr depressiv und ängstlich, und ich hatte das Gefühl, alles zu verlieren. Die Erfahrung hat mir gezeigt, dass ich stark bin und dass ich geliebt werde, von meinen Kindern, meinen Eltern und meinen Freundinnen. Das hat mir sehr geholfen. Heute geht es mir gut. Ich habe ein neues Leben aufgebaut, in einer neuen Wohnung, mit einem neuen Job, und ich bin stolz darauf. Ich bin auch dankbarer für die kleinen Dinge im Leben, die ich früher als selbstverständlich angesehen habe. Ich spüre mehr Liebe, für meine Kinder, für mich selbst und sogar ein bisschen für meinen Ex-Mann, mit dem ich jetzt ein respektvolles Verhältnis habe. Das hätte ich mir vor ein paar Jahren nicht vorstellen können.

MH06_01: I'm much better at communicating when I'm stressed. Before, I would snap at my partner and then not explain why. Now I tell her when I've had a bad day and what I need, which is usually just some quiet time. We fight a lot less because of this. I also feel more able to talk to my colleagues when there's a problem instead of stewing about it.
MH07_01: I feel much more connected and loved in my relationship, and that has made a big difference to my mental health. I'm less lonely and less anxious, and I feel like I can be myself with my partner.

MH06_01: Ich bin gelassener und kann mit stressigen Situationen besser umgehen. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr so leicht aus der Ruhe bringen und behalte eher den Überblick.
MH07_01: Ich bin ruhiger und gelassener geworden, und das tut meiner psychischen Gesundheit gut. Ich fühle mich ausgeglichener und zufriedener.

MH06_01: Honestly I don't know. The experience was more about having fun with friends than anything therapeutic.
MH07_01: Probably none. It was fun though.

MH06_01: Nothing changed in that area for me.
MH07_01: Same as before, nothing to report

MH06_01: Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, auf meinen Körper zu hören. Früher habe ich Stress immer ignoriert, bis ich krank wurde. Jetzt merke ich früher, wenn ich angespannt bin, z.B. an Verspannungen im Nacken oder an Schlafproblemen. Dann nehme ich mir bewusst Zeit für Entspannung, gehe in die Sauna oder mache einen langen Spaziergang. Das hilft mir, nicht wieder in eine Überlastung zu rutschen.
MH07_01: Ich bin psychisch stabiler, seit ich besser auf meinen Körper höre. Ich hatte früher oft depressive Phasen nach stressigen Zeiten, weil ich mich völlig verausgabt hatte. Das ist seltener geworden. Ich habe gelernt, rechtzeitig Pausen zu machen, und das tut mir sehr gut. Ich bin auch zufriedener und genieße die ruhigen Zeiten mehr. Ich verstehe jetzt besser, wie eng Körper und Psyche zusammenhängen, und das hat meine Einstellung zu Gesundheit verändert. Ich gehe regelmäßig in die Sauna und mache lange Spaziergänge im Wald, und ich merke, wie gut mir das tut. Insgesamt geht es mir viel besser als vor der Erfahrung.

MH06_01: Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, dass schwierige Situationen zum Leben dazugehören und dass ich sie nicht vermeiden muss. Früher habe ich mich bei Problemen sofort zurückgezogen, habe mich krankgemeldet oder bin Konflikten aus dem Weg gegangen. Während der Erfahrung musste ich durch eine sehr schwierige Phase hindurch, in der ich große Angst hatte, und habe gemerkt, dass es auf der anderen Seite besser wird, wenn ich nicht weglaufe. Das versuche ich seitdem im Alltag umzusetzen. Als letztes Jahr mein Vater schwer krank wurde, war ich für ihn da und habe mich der Situation gestellt, statt in Panik zu geraten. Ich habe auch gelernt, mit meiner Familie offener über Sorgen zu sprechen, und wir haben uns gegenseitig sehr unterstützt. Ich sehe belastende Ereignisse jetzt eher als Teil eines größeren Ganzen, die mich wachsen lassen.
MH07_01: Die Erfahrung hat meine psychische Gesundheit sehr positiv beeinflusst. Ich hatte vorher oft depressive Phasen, in denen ich mich leer und wertlos gefühlt habe. Während der Erfahrung habe ich eine tiefe Liebe gespürt, für mich selbst, für meine Familie und für alles Lebendige. Ich hatte das Gefühl, mit allem verbunden zu sein und nie wirklich allein zu sein. Dieses Gefühl ist geblieben, nicht so intensiv wie damals, aber es ist da, wenn ich es brauche. Ich bin dankbarer für mein Leben, für meine Gesundheit und meine Freunde, und ich genieße die kleinen Dinge viel mehr. Die depressiven Phasen sind seltener geworden und nicht mehr so tief.

MH06_01: I've stopped trying to numb my stress. Before the experience I smoked weed every evening to wind down, and I thought it helped. During the experience I saw that the weed was just covering up a lot of anxiety and sadness that never got dealt with. I quit a few weeks later. It was rough at first, I was more anxious and couldn't sleep well. But now, a year later, I deal with stress much better. I exercise, I talk to my girlfriend, and I let myself feel things. I'm less foggy and I actually solve problems instead of avoiding them.
MH07_01: Since quitting weed, my mental health has improved a lot. I'm less foggy, less anxious, and I have more energy. The first few months were hard, but now I feel clearer and more present. I understand myself better too. I see that I was using weed to avoid feelings I didn't want to deal with, and I'm learning to face them instead. My relationship with my girlfriend has improved, and I feel more connected to her.

MH06_01: I've been much better at dealing with stress at university since the experience. I used to have panic attacks before exams and I almost dropped out in my second year. During the experience I had a strong sense that my worth isn't tied to my grades, and that I'm loved regardless of what I achieve. It sounds simple but it really helped. I still get nervous before exams, but I don't panic anymore. I also started going to the university counselling service, which has helped.
MH07_01: My anxiety has improved a lot. I used to have panic attacks regularly and I almost dropped out of uni because of them. Now they're rare. I feel more confident in myself, and I've realised that I'm more than my grades. I'm more open to enjoying my student life, I've joined a few societies and made some good friends.

MH06_01: The experience gave me a sense of perspective that I didn't have before. I used to worry about everything: money, my career, what people think of me, my health, climate change. During the experience, I felt that I'm part of something eternal and that my small worries, while real, are not the whole story. Now when something stressful happens, I can step back and see it from a distance. I remind myself that I've survived everything so far, and that most of what I worried about in the past never happened. This doesn't make problems disappear, but it makes them feel more manageable, and I have more energy to actually deal with them instead of just worrying.
MH07_01: I would say the main effect on my mental health is a new appreciation for life. I used to be anxious and pessimistic, always expecting the worst. Since the experience I'm much more able to enjoy what I have. I notice beauty in everyday things, I laugh more, and I feel grateful when I wake up in the morning. That's quite a change for someone who used to dread every day. I think I also worry less because I have a sense that life is good, even with all its difficulties. My friends say I seem lighter.

MH06_01: Ich nehme mir in stressigen Zeiten bewusster Zeit für mich, z.B. für einen Spaziergang oder ein heißes Bad. Früher hätte ich das als Zeitverschwendung empfunden.
MH07_01: Ich bin entspannter und gönne mir mehr. Das tut mir gut und ich bin zufriedener mit meinem Leben.

MH06_01: I've learned to set limits and say no. That alone has made my life a lot less stressful, and I'm not exhausted all the time anymore.
MH07_01: I'm less exhausted and more balanced, and I feel better about myself. Setting limits has really helped my mental health.

MH06_01: I've become much better at handling the stress of my job as a social worker. I work with families in crisis, and I used to take everything home with me. I couldn't sleep, I'd think about the kids I work with constantly, and I was on the edge of burnout. During the experience I felt a sense of being part of something larger, like I'm one small part of a big web of people trying to help. I'm not responsible for saving everyone. That has made a big difference. I still care deeply, but I can leave work at work.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot. I was close to burnout, and I had started to feel numb and cynical about my work, which scared me, because I've always been passionate about it. Since the experience I've regained my sense of purpose and my compassion, without the overwhelming feeling of responsibility. I'm less anxious, I sleep better, and I'm more present with my own family. I also appreciate my life more, and I'm grateful for my own privileges, which I see more clearly after working with families in crisis. I feel a deep love for the work and the people I work with, and I'm more open to trusting my colleagues and the system, instead of feeling like I have to do everything myself.

MH06_01: I got better at recognising my emotions under stress. Before I would just feel 'bad', now I can tell if it's fear, sadness, anger or shame, and that helps me know what to do.
MH07_01: I feel emotionally more mature. I know what I feel and why, and that has helped me be more stable and less reactive.

MH06_01: Before, every stressful event felt like proof that my life was falling apart. I had a deep belief that I'm unlucky and that bad things always happen to me. Now when something stressful happens, I try to see it as just an event, not as part of a pattern of doom. It's made me much more resilient.
MH07_01: My depression has lifted a lot. I used to feel hopeless and unlucky, and I think that belief was a big part of my depression. Seeing it as just a story has given me a lot of freedom. MH06_01: Durch die Erfahrung habe ich gelernt, mehr im Moment zu leben. Ich mache mir weniger Sorgen um die Zukunft und kann mich besser auf das konzentrieren, was gerade wichtig ist. Das hilft mir, in stressigen Phasen nicht den Überblick zu verlieren.
MH07_01: Ich bin weniger ängstlich und kann mein Leben mehr genießen. Ich mache mir weniger Sorgen um die Zukunft und bin dankbarer für das, was ich jetzt habe.

MH06_01: Ich bin in Stresssituationen viel ruhiger als früher. Ich arbeite im Rettungsdienst, und gerade in Notfällen ist es wichtig, einen klaren Kopf zu behalten. MH07_01: Ich bin psychisch stabiler und kann die belastenden Erlebnisse aus meinem Beruf besser verarbeiten. Ich habe weniger Albträume und bin nicht mehr so angespannt. Ich bin auch dankbarer für mein eigenes Leben, weil ich im Beruf oft sehe, wie schnell es vorbei sein kann.

MH06_01: Since the experience I deal with stress by asking myself what I can control and what I can't. If I can control it, I take action. If I can't, I try to let it go. This simple question has changed my life. During the experience I saw how much energy I waste on things I can't change, like other people's opinions, the economy, the weather. Now I'm more focused and less anxious. It's helped me through a difficult job search and a health scare.
MH07_01: I'm much less anxious and more focused. I don't waste energy worrying about things I can't control, and that has made a huge difference to my mental health. I feel more at peace, and I enjoy my life more. I'm also more grateful for what I have, because I'm not constantly worried about losing it.

MH06_01: The experience helped me get some distance from my own drama. I'm a pretty emotional person, and I used to get swept away by every little thing. During the experience I was able to watch my emotions like weather passing through, and I've been able to do a bit of that since. It doesn't mean I don't feel things, I still feel them strongly, but I don't get as lost in them. When my partner and I had a big fight recently, I was able to step back and see that I was reacting out of fear, and I could tell him that, instead of just yelling. We made up the same day, which never used to happen.
MH07_01: I'm more emotionally stable and better at managing my mood swings. I understand my emotions better, I can name them and see where they come from. MH07_01: Mir geht es besser, seit ich mehr auf mich achte. Meine Kopfschmerzen sind seltener geworden, und ich bin insgesamt ausgeglichener.

MH06_01: Ich bin ruhiger und gelassener geworden. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr so leicht provozieren und kann in schwierigen Gesprächen sachlich bleiben.
MH07_01: Ich bin ruhiger und ausgeglichener. Mir geht es gut.

MH06_01: The way I handle stress is completely different now, and I think it comes down to one thing: I'm no longer trying to escape from myself. Before the experience I was always running, from my feelings, from my past, from silence. I filled every moment with work, podcasts, social media, drinks with friends. When something stressful happened, I'd just run faster. During the experience I couldn't run anymore. I had to sit with everything, and it was terrifying at first, but then it became peaceful. I realised that underneath all the running there was a deep loneliness and a feeling that I'm not enough. Once I saw that, I couldn't unsee it. Now I try to stop and feel when I'm stressed instead of running. I go for walks without headphones. I sit with a cup of tea and just notice what's happening inside. I've also cut back on drinking. It's harder in some ways because I feel more, but I'm much more stable. I don't get the big crashes I used to get after months of running on empty.
MH07_01: My mental health is much better since I stopped running from myself. I used to have periods of burnout and depression every year or so, usually after months of overworking and overdrinking. Since the experience I haven't had one, and it's been almost three years. I'm more emotionally honest, I feel my feelings, and that keeps them from building up. I've also become much more appreciative of quiet and simple things. I used to be bored and restless whenever I wasn't busy, and now I can enjoy a slow morning or an evening reading. I'm more open to my own inner world, my dreams, my intuitions, which I used to dismiss. And I've found that I'm actually good company for myself, which I never believed before. I'm much happier now, though it's a quieter kind of happiness than I expected.

MH06_01: Ich habe gelernt, dass ich nicht perfekt sein muss. Das hat mir viel Stress genommen, sowohl im Beruf als auch im Privatleben.
MH07_01: Ich bin entspannter und weniger selbstkritisch. Das hat meine Stimmung verbessert, und ich bin zufriedener mit mir und meinem Leben.

MH07_01: I'm less angry and more emotionally stable. I understand myself better, and my relationship with my son has improved.

MH06_01: I've stopped using avoidance as a coping strategy. I used to ignore problems until they became crises, unpaid bills, health issues, relationship stuff. The experience made me see that avoiding is actually more stressful than facing things. Now I deal with things as they come, which means I'm less stressed overall. I opened all my unopened letters the week after the trip, which was terrifying but felt amazing afterwards.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved because I'm not constantly carrying the weight of everything I've been avoiding. I used to have a background anxiety all the time, and I didn't know where it came from. After I started dealing with things, it lifted. I'm calmer, I sleep better and I'm more productive. MH06_01: I'm a teacher and the experience changed how I deal with difficult students and parents. I used to take everything personally and get defensive. It doesn't mean I don't set boundaries, but I don't feel attacked anymore, and I'm much calmer at work. My headteacher has commented on it.
MH07_01: I'm much less burnt out and more satisfied with my job. I feel more compassion and love, not just for my students, but for people in general, and that has made me happier. I'm also more open to new teaching methods and ideas, which has made my job more interesting again. I used to dread Mondays, and now I mostly look forward to seeing the kids.

MH06_01: I've been through a really stressful period since the experience: my partner was diagnosed with MS, I had to take on more work to cover our income, and my father went into a care home. Looking back, I'm amazed at how I coped. I think the experience gave me a deep sense that I can hold difficult things without collapsing. During the trip I went through waves of fear and grief that felt unbearable, and each time I let them wash over me, they passed. So when the diagnosis came, I let myself be scared and sad, and I didn't try to fix everything immediately. I also asked for help, which I never used to do. Friends brought food, my sister came for a week, and I joined a support group for partners of people with MS. I'm not saying it's been easy. There were nights when I cried in the bathroom so my partner wouldn't hear. But I never felt completely lost, and I've managed to stay present for her and for myself.
MH07_01: It's hard to separate the effects of the experience from everything that's happened since, but I'd say my mental health has held up remarkably well under circumstances that would have broken me before. The main thing is that I feel a deep love for my partner and for life that carries me. During the experience, I felt that love is the ground we stand on, and that everything else is weather. I still feel that. When I'm with my partner on a hard day, when her legs don't work or she's exhausted, I feel sad, but I also feel this enormous tenderness and gratitude that we have each other. I appreciate small things so much more: a good day when she has energy, a walk together, a meal with friends. I've had moments of despair, of course, but I haven't fallen into depression, which I've had twice in my life before. I think the experience gave me a kind of foundation, and the people around me have built on it.

MH06_01: Durch die Erfahrung habe ich gelernt, meine Stressreaktionen besser zu verstehen. Ich habe während der Erfahrung gesehen, wie mein Körper auf Angst reagiert: Mein Bauch zieht sich zusammen, meine Schultern gehen hoch, ich halte den Atem an. Das hatte ich vorher nie bemerkt. Jetzt erkenne ich diese Signale im Alltag früher und kann gegensteuern, indem ich bewusst atme, die Schultern fallen lasse und mich kurz zurückziehe. Ich habe außerdem verstanden, dass mein Stress oft mit dem Gefühl zusammenhängt, nicht gut genug zu sein, und dass dieses Gefühl aus meiner Kindheit stammt, als mein Vater sehr hohe Erwartungen an mich hatte. Mit diesem Wissen kann ich in belastenden Situationen freundlicher mit mir sein. Ich habe auch angefangen, regelmäßig zu meditieren, was mir sehr hilft. Insgesamt bin ich viel besser in der Lage, mit Stress umzugehen, auch wenn es immer noch Momente gibt, in denen ich in alte Muster falle.
MH07_01: Ich habe durch die Erfahrung ein viel besseres Verständnis für mich selbst entwickelt. Ich weiß jetzt, warum ich so hohe Ansprüche an mich habe und warum ich mich so schnell schlecht fühle, wenn ich sie nicht erfülle. Das hat mir geholfen, freundlicher mit mir umzugehen. Die Meditation, die ich seitdem regelmäßig mache, hilft mir, bei mir zu bleiben und meine Gedanken nicht so ernst zu nehmen. Ich habe danach auch eine Therapie gemacht, in der ich vieles vertiefen konnte, was in der Erfahrung aufgetaucht ist.

MH06_01: I'm a nurse in an emergency department, and the experience helped me cope with the trauma I'd been accumulating at work. I hadn't realised how much I'd been storing up until the experience brought it all out. During the trip I saw faces of patients I'd lost, children, young people, people who died alone. I cried for hours. It was awful, but afterwards I felt lighter than I had in years. Since then, I've been better at processing the hard shifts. I talk to my colleagues about what we've seen, we do debriefs, and I've started seeing a therapist who specialises in healthcare workers. I've also learned to leave work at work. I have a little ritual when I take off my scrubs: I imagine putting the day in my locker. It helps. I'm less irritable at home and my partner says I'm more present.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved a lot since the experience. I had been showing signs of PTSD from my work in the ED, things like nightmares, irritability, and a kind of numbness, though I didn't recognise it at the time. I thought it was just part of the job. The experience brought all of that to the surface, and since then I've been able to process it. My nightmares have mostly stopped. I'm less irritable and more present with my partner and my friends. I feel things again, which is both good and hard. I've also become more compassionate towards myself. I used to think I had to be tough to do my job, but now I see that being able to feel is what makes me good at it. I'm grateful for the experience and for the therapist I've been seeing, who has helped me integrate it.

MH06_01: The experience was at a time when I was dealing with a lot of stress from caring for my mother with dementia, working full time, and raising two teenagers. I felt like I was drowning. During the experience I saw myself as a tree in a storm, bending but not breaking, with deep roots. That image has stayed with me. When I'm overwhelmed now, I think of that tree, and I remind myself that I can bend without breaking. I've also learned to accept that I can't do everything perfectly. Some days the house is a mess, dinner is pizza, and I don't call my sister back. That's okay. I've also asked my brother to take on more responsibility for our mother, which I was too proud to do before, and he has stepped up. I feel less alone in it now.
MH07_01: I was close to a breakdown before the experience. I was exhausted, crying in the car, snapping at everyone. The experience gave me a sense of strength and also a lot of love, for my mother, for my kids, for myself. I realised I'd forgotten to love myself in all of this. Since then I take a little time for myself every day, even if it's just ten minutes with a cup of tea in the garden. My mental health is much better, I'm less depressed and anxious, and I can enjoy moments with my family even when things are hard. I also appreciate my mother in a new way. Even though she doesn't know who I am most days, there are still moments of connection, a smile, a hand squeeze, and I cherish those now instead of only grieving what's lost.

MH06_01: I see things more in perspective now. Problems at work feel less important compared to the big questions of life. That helps me not get too stressed out, though sometimes it also makes me care less about doing a good job.
MH07_01: I felt great for a while, more relaxed and positive. But after a couple of months it wore off and I went back to how I was before.

MH06_01: My psychedelic experience was a very difficult one, a bad trip at a party where I felt that I was dying and that everyone was against me. I know what it feels like to be at the absolute bottom, and I know I can come back. When I face stressful situations now, I remind myself of that. But it was a long road to get here.
MH07_01: At first it was really bad for my mental health. I had anxiety, panic attacks and I avoided crowds for over a year. I was afraid I'd broken something in my brain. With therapy, I slowly got better, and now I think I'm actually more resilient and self-aware than before. But I wouldn't recommend going through it the way I did.

MH06_01: I've had a lot of stress in my life since the experience: my wife and I separated, I lost my job during a restructuring, and I had to move back to my hometown. It has been the hardest two years of my life. I think the experience has helped me get through it in a few ways. First, it gave me a sense of perspective. During the trip I felt like I was looking at my whole life from above, and I saw that it's long and full of chapters, and that the difficult ones are just as much a part of the story as the happy ones. Second, it made me more open to my emotions. I used to just push through and never talk about how I felt. During the separation, I actually cried, I talked to my brother and my old friends, and I even went to a counsellor for a few months. I think that's why I didn't fall into a deep depression like my dad did when he went through something similar. I'm still rebuilding, but I'm hopeful.
MH07_01: My mental health has been tested a lot in the last two years, and I think it held up better than it would have without the experience. I've had some low periods, especially after the separation, but I haven't fallen into a deep depression, which has happened to me before and which happened to my dad. I think the main reason is that I'm more open now, with my emotions and with other people. I let my friends and family support me, and I talk about how I feel instead of bottling it up. I also appreciate the good things in my life more: my kids, who I see every other weekend, my brother, the hills around my hometown where I go walking. I've rediscovered a lot of old friendships since moving back. I'm still finding my way, but I feel hopeful about the future, and I think I'm becoming a more open and honest person.

MH06_01: For me, the experience was mostly about grief. My twin brother died by suicide four years ago, and I had never really grieved him. I just kept going, working long hours, never talking about it. During the experience, I felt his presence very strongly. I don't know if it was really him or something my mind created, but it doesn't matter. He told me it wasn't my fault and that he wanted me to live. I sobbed for hours. Since then, I've been able to talk about him, with my parents, with friends, and with a grief counsellor. I've also become much better at dealing with other stressful things, because I'm not carrying that huge weight around anymore. Before, any small stress would push me to the edge, because I was already full. Now there's more room inside me. I've started volunteering for a suicide prevention line, which is hard but also gives me a sense of meaning.
MH07_01: The experience was the beginning of healing after my brother's death. For four years I'd been numb and depressed, though I didn't really admit it. I was functioning, but I wasn't living. I had nightmares and I couldn't look at photos of him. After the experience I was able to grieve, and slowly the numbness lifted. I can feel joy again, and love. I can look at his photos and smile. My depression has improved a lot, and I don't have nightmares anymore. I've also become much closer to my parents, because we talk about him together now. I feel a deep gratitude for the time I had with him, and for being alive. I appreciate my life in a way I didn't before, maybe because I know how fragile it is. Volunteering on the crisis line gives me a sense of purpose. I feel like I'm honouring him by helping others.

MH06_01: I'm better at dealing with my depression when it hits. I used to think it would last forever and that made it worse. Now I know from experience that it passes, and I can wait it out with self-care.
MH07_01: My depression still comes and goes, but it's less frightening now and the episodes are shorter. I know they pass. That knowledge alone has helped a lot.

MH06_01: Since the experience I have been a lot more accepting of the stressful situations that I can't change, for example my mother's illness and my financial worries. I can feel the worry without being consumed by it. I think the experience taught me that feelings come and go, and that I don't have to hold on to them or push them away. Life is less of a battle now.
MH07_01: I'm much more at peace. I used to be very anxious and always worried about something, and now I feel a sense of calm underneath it all. I appreciate my life much more and I'm grateful for small things, like being able to have coffee with my mum, even though she's sick. I think the experience showed me that every moment is precious and that I don't have to wait for things to be perfect to be happy.

MH07_01: I'm less exhausted and more balanced. I take better care of my energy.

MH06_01: Ich gehe heute offener mit meinen Gefühlen um, wenn ich gestresst bin. Ich sage zum Beispiel meinem Partner, dass ich gerade überfordert bin, statt einfach schlecht gelaunt zu sein. Das macht vieles einfacher.
MH07_01: Ich fühle mich in meiner Beziehung verstandener und unterstützter, und das hat meine Stimmung sehr verbessert. Ich bin weniger einsam und weniger ängstlich, weil ich nicht mehr alles mit mir allein ausmache. Ich spüre auch mehr Nähe und Liebe zu meinem Partner.

MH06_01: Before the experience, my reaction to stress was to drink and smoke. I'd come home from work and have a few beers and a joint just to switch off. During the experience I saw how I was numbing myself, and that the stress was still there underneath, just pushed away. I've since cut down on both, and I go to the gym or play guitar instead. It's harder in the moment because I actually have to feel the stress, but in the long run I feel much better and I deal with problems instead of avoiding them.
MH07_01: My mental health has improved since I cut down on alcohol and weed. I'm less depressed and more clear-headed. I also understand myself better, I know now that I was self-medicating for anxiety, and I've started seeing a doctor about it.

MH06_01: Ich bin weniger ängstlich, wenn es um die Zukunft geht. Ich vertraue mehr darauf, dass ich mit dem, was kommt, umgehen kann. Das hat mir viel Druck genommen.
MH07_01: Ich bin weniger ängstlich und zuversichtlicher geworden. Ich habe das Gefühl, dass ich mit dem Leben besser zurechtkomme.

MH06_01: Ich habe während der Erfahrung sehr deutlich gesehen, wie sehr ich mich in meinem Leben von Angst habe leiten lassen. Ich habe einen sicheren Beruf gewählt, den ich nicht mag, ich bin in einer Stadt geblieben, in der ich mich nicht wohlfühle, und ich habe mich nie getraut, meine Meinung zu sagen. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, wie viel Leben ich dadurch verpasst habe, und ich habe auch gespürt, dass ich den Mut habe, etwas zu ändern. Seitdem habe ich einiges verändert. Ich habe eine Weiterbildung angefangen, um mich beruflich neu zu orientieren, und ich plane, im nächsten Jahr umzuziehen. Diese Veränderungen sind natürlich auch mit Stress verbunden, aber es ist ein anderer Stress. Es ist der Stress von jemandem, der sein Leben selbst gestaltet, nicht der Stress von jemandem, der sich ständig vor allem fürchtet. Mit belastenden Situationen gehe ich heute mutiger um. Ich gehe Probleme an, statt sie zu vermeiden, und ich vertraue darauf, dass ich Lösungen finden werde.
MH07_01: Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung sehr verbessert. Ich war lange Zeit unzufrieden und hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Leben an mir vorbeizieht. Ich hatte depressive Verstimmungen und eine ständige innere Unruhe, die ich mir nicht erklären konnte. Heute weiß ich, dass diese Unruhe daher kam, dass ich nicht das Leben gelebt habe, das ich leben wollte. Seit ich angefangen habe, mein Leben zu verändern, geht es mir viel besser. Ich bin zufriedener, mutiger und offener für Neues. Ich habe Freude an meiner Weiterbildung und freue mich auf den Umzug. Ich verstehe mich selbst besser und weiß, was mir wichtig ist. Ich bin auch dankbarer für mein Leben, weil ich gemerkt habe, dass ich es selbst gestalten kann. Das gibt mir ein Gefühl von Freiheit, das ich vorher nicht kannte.
